then official duties become lowly and without stipends.
Externally, skins and silks are not worn in the realm;
internally, the state's duties are lowly.
Liáng Jù's words are wrong.
You, the ruler, possess mountains,
and the mountains have metal, which is used to establish currency.
By using currency to standardize grain and bestow stipends,
the state's grain will remain with the superior,
and the price of grain will increase tenfold.
Farmers will sleep late and rise early, not waiting to be commanded;
the production of five grains will increase tenfold.
Scholars will die for the ruler even for half a stipend;
farmers will sleep late and rise early,
working hard without ceasing.
Those good at governing a state
do not say they are commanding them,
but make it so they cannot but be commanded.
They do not say they are using them,
but make it so they cannot but be used.
Thus, they make it so there is no one among the people who cannot but be commanded.
Indeed, Liáng Jù's words are wrong."
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng again asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"There is someone who taught me,
calling himself an 'invited scholar'.
He said:
'Why not appoint officials for a hundred abilities?'"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"What is meant by 'a hundred abilities'?"
Huán Gōng said:
"Making the wise exhaust their wisdom,
the strategists exhaust their plans,
and the various artisans exhaust their skills.
If it is like this, can the state be governed?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The invited scholar's words are wrong.
When stipends are rich, scholars will not die for the cause;
when currency is light, scholars will disparage rewards;
when all things are light, scholars will be opportunistic.
When these three forms of negligence exist in the state,
what strategy is there?
If seven-tenths of the grain are stored above
and three-tenths circulate below,
strategists will exhaust their considerations,
wise men will exhaust their knowledge,
and brave men will treat death lightly.
What the invited scholar said is a reckless statement.
Not being well-versed in the 'light and heavy' strategy,
it is called a reckless statement."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"In the past, the Zhōu people possessed the realm,
the Zhūhóu submitted as guests,
and their reputation and teachings spread through the realm,
yet they were deprived of power by those below.
What strategy was this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The ruler divided the land and received tribute,
while the market and the court shared the same flow.
Gold was one strategy;
the pearls of Jiāngyáng were one strategy;
the malachite of Míngshān in Qín was one strategy.
This is called 'using the few to represent the many'
and 'using the narrow to represent the broad'.
These belong to the category of 'light and heavy'."
Huán Gōng said:
"Does the strategy of the realm consist entirely of the category of light
and heavy?"
Guǎn Zǐ said: "Now, if the state's grain is ten times as heavy while all things are light,
the Dàfū will say to the merchants: 'You transport grain for me and collect wealth.'
When the weight of grain is one,
now nine parts are in excess.
When grain is heavy and all things are light,
like this,
then nine parts of the state's wealth will be with the Dàfū.
When the state's cycle returns to one,
the nine parts of wealth and goods
will all be released at double the weight.
While goods are with those below,
nine parts of the currency are with the Dàfū.
Thus, both currency and grain surpluses are with the Dàfū.
The Tiānzǐ conducts himself as a guest;
his commands are issued seasonally.
Those skilled in grain production will flee,
the Zhūhóu will receive them and give them official posts.
They form factions and gather associates,
raising and lowering the value of all things
to suit the people's needs.
Internally, the Dàfū
look to their own interests and are not fully loyal;
externally, the Zhūhóu form factions and gather associates.
Those skilled in grain production then leave and flee.
Thus, the Tiānzǐ loses his power."
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng again asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"To possess the world throughout one's life without losing it,
is there a Way to achieve this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Please do not apply it to the whole world yet;
apply it solely to our state."
Huán Gōng said:
"What do you mean by these words?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The width and narrowness of the state
and the fertility or barrenness of the soil
have their fixed measures,
and the surplus of food at the end of the year also has its measure.
Those who guard a state merely guard its grain.
If it is said: 'The soil of a certain county is so wide,
and the soil of a certain county is so narrow,'
then one must accumulate and entrust currency,
so that these counties, districts, and villages receive public money.
In mid-autumn, when the state's grain has decreased by one-third,
the lord should issue an order telling the commanderies, counties, and subordinate dà fū
in the villages to each register and collect a certain amount of grain.
When the grain price is uniform,
use it to store wealth with the superior. When the state's grain is divided into three parts,
then two parts will be held by the superior.
In mid-spring, the state's grain will double in value; this is a matter of calculation.
In mid-summer,
distribute grain to adjust market prices,
and the people will all receive grain from the superior to cultivate their fields.
In mid-autumn,
it should be said:
'The amount of grain the people owe to me is such-and-such;
now the superior will collect grain using currency.'
The people will say: 'We have no currency;
we will pay in grain.'
Thus, three parts of the people's harvest will return to the superior.
The interaction of high and low prices
and the timely implementation of changes
are all state strategies.
The lord uses the stores of the dà fū to let wealth flow back to the superior.
The lord employs the people so that they return wealth to the lord according to the seasons.
To store when prices are low and release when prices are high is the calculation.
Then how could those self-serving dà fū monopolize their own stores?
If the grain of the zhū hóu is at ten
and we make our state's grain twenty,
then the grain of the zhū hóu will flow into our state.
If the grain of the zhū hóu is at twenty
and our state's grain is at ten,
then our state's grain will flow out to the zhū hóu.
Therefore, those who are skilled at managing the world
carefully guard the flow of values,
so that the world's wealth does not leak away from us.
High prices gravitating toward each other
is like water flowing downward.
Even if our state does not have a bad harvest year,
by storing wealth with currency,
the state's grain will double in value,
and thus the grain of the zhū hóu will arrive.
This is storing one part to attract one part from the zhū hóu.
Profit is not snatched from the world,
and the dà fū cannot become extravagantly wealthy.
By using the heavy to store the light,
the state will always possess the strategies of ten states.
Therefore, the zhū hóu submit without ceasing,
and the ministers follow with loyalty.
This is the Way of governing the world through the 'heavy and light';
it is called the 'correspondence of calculations'."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"I ask about the state assembly of accounts."
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"If the lord loses the dà fū, he has no peers;
if he loses the people, he loses his foundation.
Therefore, control the dà fū with the strategy of the county;
control a county with the strategy of a township;
control a township with the strategy of a household;
control a household with the strategy of an individual."
Huán Gōng said:
"What are the calculations for these accounts?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"In the calculation of currency standards,
a county must have a strategy for its medium-quality fields,
a township must have a strategy for its medium-quality fields,
and a household must have the utility of its labor.
Thus, failing to control the commanderies according to the seasons means having no participation;
failing to control the townships according to the seasons means having no organization."
Huán Gōng said:
"How do we implement this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"A true King stores wealth among the people;
a Hegemon stores wealth among the dà fū;
a ruinous state or a dying house stores wealth in mere strategies."
Huán Gōng said:
"What is meant by storing wealth among the people?"
Guǎn Zǐ said: "I request that
the money from Zhàn Tái
be distributed in Chéng Yáng,
and the cloth from Lù Tái
be distributed in Jì Yīn.
The lord should issue an order to the common people, saying:
'When the people are wealthy, the lord will not share their poverty;
when the people are poor, the lord will not share their wealth.'
Thus, taxes will not consist of money or cloth,
the treasury will not store goods,
and wealth will be stored among the people.
In a bumper year when the five grains are harvested,
the five grains become very cheap.
When the grain price drops compared to the previous year, use currency to secure it.
Grain then becomes the primary value
and currency becomes the secondary.
The state's currency will all be among the common people;
currency will be light, and the grain held by the superior will be heavy.
Two parts of the previous year's wealth are below,
and two parts of the following year's wealth are above;
thus four parts from two years are held by the superior.
Then one part of the state's grain remains below,
and the grain becomes three times as heavy.
Regarding the registration of state cloth,
it is ten coins for the whole year.
When a household receives food, for every ten mǔ add ten;
this is ten households per family.
This arises from the state grain strategy and is stored in currency.
Use the portions of state currency to redistribute to the common people again,
reducing the state grain by four parts:
three are held by the superior,
and one remains below.
This is the returning strategy.
When the dà fū travel together and are granted fiefs,
they accumulate goods and are arrogant toward the superior;
please take this from them through the assembly of accounts."
Huán Gōng said:
"What is meant by taking it from them through the assembly of accounts?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"With three parts of the grain held by the superior,
tell the common people that they all receive grain from the superior,
as measured by the lord's stores.
When the five grains interact and become heavy,
remove three-tenths; for the rest,
use the state currency and grain standards to circulate them back.
The dà fū will have no way to profit from high prices.
The lord uses currency to distribute stipends,
and ten parts are held by the superior.
When the lord releases grain, seven parts out of ten are removed.
The lord collects three parts,
and the superior distributes seven.
Distributing aid to those without resources
is benevolence and righteousness.
When the five grains interact and become cheap,
it is a matter of calculation;
using the township to control the heavy and tax the state
is a matter of calculation;
releasing material wealth
and dispersing benevolence and righteousness
so that all things become light
is a matter of calculation.
Advance or retreat according to the timing.
Therefore it is said:
'A King takes advantage of the time;
a Sage takes advantage of changes.'"
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"It was specifically commanded to me:
'The Son of Heaven has three hundred officials,
which is extremely frugal.
But if the dà fū are dispersed
and follow this standard,'
what of this?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"This is not the way of those who manage the state by law.
If the dà fū raise their burial mounds
and beautify their houses,
this snatches away labor from farming and the markets;
this is not the way to benefit the state."
The people must not be allowed to weave raw or fine silk
and bury it in the ground.
Those who are good at governing a state
merely ride the timings of slow and fast economic cycles.
This is called the Guó Huì (National Accounting). 」
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"May I ask about the matter of contention and seizure?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"It begins with relatives. 」
Huán Gōng said:
"What do you mean by 'beginning with relatives'?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"As a ruler of men,
if one has ten brothers,
the state is divided into ten;
if there are five brothers,
the state is divided into five.
By the third generation, they share the same ancestor in the Zhāo and Mù order;
by the tenth generation, they are merely tablets in the Shí shrine.
Thus, fallen corpses fill the fields,
and warfare breaks out without ceasing.
Experts in the 'Light and Heavy'
then wander among them.
Therefore it is said:
'Do not give land to others,
and do not grant wealth to others.'
When wealth ends, it begins anew,
fading and rising with the four seasons.
Sages manage this through slow and fast pacing,
maintain it through opening and closing,
seize it through the 'Light and Heavy,'
and implement it through benevolence and righteousness.
Thus they share the same lifespan as heaven and earth;
this is the Great Reins of a King. 」
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"May I ask about the Bì Chéng Mǎ (Currency Multiplied by Horses). 」
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Begin by taking households of three adult males;
for every six square lǐ, there is one Chéng (chariot unit),
with twenty-seven men supporting one Chéng.
Regarding Bì Chéng Mǎ,
within six square lǐ,
based on whether the land is poor or fertile,
the quantity of grain produced,
and the high or low price of grain,
calculate how much currency should be used for each six square lǐ,
and how much currency
corresponds to the weight of the grain.
Therefore, for Bì Chéng Mǎ,
distribute currency throughout the state;
let the currency correspond to the total calculation of the state's land resources;
this is called Bì Chéng Mǎ. 」
Huán Gōng said:
"How is the method of Bì Chéng Mǎ implemented? 」
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Officers receive their capital in currency,
Dàfū receive their fiefs in currency,
and the rations for men and horses are received in currency.
Thus, the state's grain resources are held above,
and the currency resources are held below.
When the state's grain increases tenfold,
it is due to this calculation.
If the value of all goods decreases by twenty percent,
it is due to this strategy.
Leather, hides, sinews, horns,
feathers, hair, bamboo, arrows,
equipment, and goods—
provided they match the state's equipment or the ruler's needs—
all shall have vouchers registered above.
The ruler should store them in the Xiāng and Zhōu.
It is said:
'On such a month and such a day,
for those who follow the requirements,
the Xiāng and Zhōu will settle the accounts.'
Therefore it is said:
'Settle the wages in one day.'
State strategies emerge from the tracking of grain;
the state's strategic goods
are managed by the Bì Chéng Mǎ method.
Currently, knives and cloth coins are stored in official treasuries,
but the clever manipulation of currency and the 'Light and Heavy' of all goods
are all in the hands of merchants.
They make currency heavy and goods light,
or currency light and goods heavy.
They make currency light and grain heavy,
or currency heavy and grain light.
If the ruler of men controls grain, currency, and the Zhǔn Héng (balancing scales),
then the world can be stabilized.
This is the method for maintaining the world. 」
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"Zhǔn Héng, the 'Light and Heavy,' and the Guó Huì—
I have heard of these.
May I ask about the Xiàn Shù (District Calculations). 」
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"From Lángmǔ to the mouth of Fénghuì,
and from Lóngxià northward
to Hǎizhuāng,
these are lands for birds, beasts, sheep, and cattle.
Why not use this to facilitate state strategies? 」
Huán Gōng said:
"What do you mean by 'facilitating state strategies'?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"At the gates of the markets in Féng Shì, have an official record the pledges
for tasks. If the tasks
of the stable-keepers and herdsmen
are performed such that the animals are raised without loss, injury, or death,
remove their capital-city duties
and their Xiàn duties.
If a Dàfū does not lead his Xiāng in these gatherings,
he is said to lack ritual and righteousness;
the Dàfū's Chūnqiū records shall be obscured,
and the common people's gates and mountain shrines shall be obscured.
When the price of oxen and sheep for sacrifice in Fénghuì and Lóngxià
becomes ten times higher than on other days,
this arises from ritual and righteousness;
it is a tax levied on otherwise useless land,
following the strategy of pens and enclosures.
This is called Facilitation. 」
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"May I ask about the Guó Shì (State Situations). 」
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"There are states situated in the mountains,
states situated in low-lying flooded areas with much water,
states with divided mountain lands,
states with overflowing waters,
and states with porous soil.
These are the five situations of states
that a ruler must worry about.
A state situated in the mountains
should always store one-third of its grain.
A state in low-lying flooded areas with much water
should always control one-third of the state's grain.
A state with divided mountain lands
should always control three-tenths of the state's grain.
Regarding damage caused by springs and water,
a state with overflowing waters
should always control two-tenths.
A state with porous soil
must carefully gather the five grains from the various feudal lords.
Employ artisans to carve patterns on catalpa wood
to bring in the five grains from the world;
this is the calculation for the five situations based on balancing the seasons. 」
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"Now that I possess all within the seas
and have made the feudal lords my subordinates,
can the Guó Shì then be dispensed with? 」
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Now, treat the feudal lords as the source
of the surplus from the public administrative districts.
Use this to ride the four seasons,
implement the strategy of pens and enclosures,
and cover the East, West, South, and North,
using leveling to achieve balance.
Therefore it is said:
'Regarding the feudal lords,
adjust the prices of all goods high or low to respond to them.'
When one possesses the whole world,
then issue currency to guard the daily fluctuations of all goods,
and simply regulate them.
If there is sufficient profit, proceed;
if it is insufficient, stop.
The King should have the Xiāng and Zhōu observe this according to the seasons;
thus profits will not overturn each other,
and the Xiàn will be secure in their places.
The ruler guards the great mandate and maintains unity;
this is called the Guó Bù (National Register). 」
Huán Gōng said:
"May I hear about the Dì Shù (Calculations of the Earth)?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The earth measures twenty-eight thousand lǐ from East to West
and twenty-six thousand lǐ from North to South.
Areas where water flows out comprise eight thousand lǐ;
areas that receive water comprise eight thousand lǐ.
There are four hundred and sixty-seven mountains that produce copper,
and three thousand six hundred and nine mountains that produce iron.
This is the reason for dividing the soil and planting grain;
it is from where spears and lances are deployed,
and where knives and coins arise.
The capable have a surplus,
while the clumsy have a deficit.
To perform the Fēng sacrifice at Tài Shān
and the Shàn sacrifice at Liáng Fù—
among the seventy-two houses
of kings who performed the Fēng Shàn sacrifices,
the reckoning of their gains and losses
are all contained within this.
This is called national expenditure.
Huán Gōng said:
“What is meant by saying the reckoning of gains and losses are all contained here?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“In the past, Jié was a hegemon who possessed the world,
yet his resources were insufficient.
Tāng possessed only the seventy lǐ of Bó,
yet his resources were more than enough.
It was not that Heaven rained down beans and grain solely for Tāng,
nor that the Earth produced wealth and goods solely for Tāng.
Yī Yǐn was skilled at circulation and shifting, the ‘light and heavy,’
opening and closing, and dredging and damming.
He was well-versed in the strategies of high and low prices and slow and fast paces,
managing them as easily as sitting down or standing up. It was a matter of utilizing timing.
Huáng Dì asked Bó Gāo:
‘I wish to mold the world into one single family;
is there a way to do this?’
Bó Gāo replied:
‘Please cut down the sedge and plant it;
if we cautiously avoid its early teeth,
then the world can be molded into one single family.’
Huáng Dì said:
‘May I hear more of these words?’
Bó Gāo replied:
‘Where there is cinnabar above,
there is gold below;
where there is magnetite above,
there is copper-gold below;
where there is líng stone above,
there is lead, tin, and red copper below;
where there is ochre above,
there is iron below.
These are the outward signs of the mountains.
If a mountain displays such signs,
the ruler should cautiously seal it off and perform sacrifices.
Build an altar ten lǐ away from the boundary.
This will cause those in carriages to dismount and walk,
and those walking to hurry.
If anyone violates the decree, they shall be punished by death without pardon.
In this way, people will keep their distance from plundering it.’
After ten years of cultivating this teaching,
Mount Gé Lú burst forth with water,
and metal followed it.
Chī Yóu took it and forged it
into swords, armor, spears, and halberds.
In that year, he annexed nine feudal lords.
Mount Yōng Hú burst forth with water,
and metal followed it.
Chī Yóu took it and forged it
into the halberds of Yōng Hú and the spears of Ruì.
In that year, he annexed twelve feudal lords.
Therefore, when the lords of the world
brandish their halberds in a single fit of rage,
fallen corpses fill the fields.
This is the origin of what is seen in weaponry.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“May I ask where the wealth of Heaven emerges
and where the benefits of the Earth lie?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Where there is ochre on a mountain,
there is iron below.
Where there is lead above,
there is silver below.
It is also said:
‘Where there is lead above,
there is zhù-silver below.
Where there is cinnabar above,
there is zhù-gold below.
Where there is magnetite above,
there is copper-gold below.’
These are the outward signs of the mountains.
If a mountain displays such signs,
cautiously seal it and establish a prohibition.
If anyone disturbs the sealed mountain,
they shall be punished by death without pardon.
As for those who violate the decree:
if the left foot enters,
the left foot is severed;
if the right foot enters,
the right foot is severed.
In this way, people will keep their distance from violating it.
This is where the wealth of Heaven and the benefits of Earth lie.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“Who were those who used the wealth of Heaven and the benefits of Earth to establish merit and achieve fame in the world?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Wén and Wǔ were such ones.”
Huán Gōng said:
“What is meant by these words?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Jade arises from the frontier mountains of Niú Shì.
Gold arises from the marshes to the right of the Rǔ and Hàn Rivers.
Pearls arise from the dim light of the edge of the Chì Yě.
These are all seven thousand eight hundred lǐ away from Zhōu.
The paths are long and arrival is difficult.
Therefore, the former kings utilized each according to its relative importance.
Pearls and jade were the high currency,
gold was the middle currency,
and knives and cloth were the low currency.
When decrees are urgent, gold is expensive.
When decrees are relaxed, gold is cheap.
The former kings weighed and measured the pace of their commands,
adjusting the value of the middle currency up or down
to regulate the usage of lower and upper currencies;
Wén and Wǔ were such kings.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“I wish to preserve the national wealth
without taxing the world,
while relying on the world externally; is this possible?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“It is possible.
When water is agitated, it flows through channels.
When decrees are urgent, goods become heavy.
The former kings managed the pace of their commands
to preserve national wealth internally
and rely on the world externally.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“How is this put into practice?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“In the past, Wǔ Wáng possessed the grain of Jù Qiáo;
this was the strategy of buying grain when it was expensive.”
Huán Gōng said:
“How was this done?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Wǔ Wáng established a garrison at Zhòng Quán
and issued an order saying:
‘Any commoner who possesses one hundred gǔ of grain is exempt from service.’
The commoners gathered their accumulated grain
to avoid the garrison duty at Zhòng Quán,
and the price of grain in the state increased twenty-fold.
The grain of Jù Qiáo also increased twenty-fold in value.
Wǔ Wáng used the twenty-fold value of the Jù Qiáo grain to purchase silk fabrics,
and for five years the army did not need to levy clothing from the people.
He used the twenty-fold value of the Jù Qiáo grain to balance one million units of gold,
and for the rest of his life, he never levied from the people.
This is the strategy of equalization and balancing.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“Can this be practiced today as well?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“It is possible.
Chǔ has the gold of Rǔ Hàn,
Qí has the salt of Qú Zhǎn,
and Yān has the salt-boiling of Liáo Dōng.
These three can also match the strategy of Wǔ Wáng.
In a household of ten,
ten people consume salt;
in a household of a hundred,
a hundred people consume salt.
Regarding the general amount of salt consumed:
in one month, an adult male consumes five and one-third shēng,
an adult female three and one-third shēng,
and an infant two and one-third shēng.
Regarding the value of salt:
if the price per shēng increases by a fraction of a hào, a fǔ becomes fifty;
if it increases by one hào, a fǔ becomes one hundred;
if it increases by ten hào, a fǔ becomes one thousand.
Your Highness should cut the brushwood
and boil the brine to make salt.
Manage and accumulate thirty thousand zhōng of it.
When Yáng Chūn arrives,
please levy based on the requirements of the time.”
Huán Gōng asked:
“What is meant by levying taxes according to the seasons?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“In the spring, when agricultural work is just beginning,
order the people not to build walls
or repair tombs;
the high officials must not construct palaces
or erect terraces and pavilions.
The masses of the Běihǎi region must not gather laborers to boil salt.
In this way, the price of salt will certainly increase forty-fold.
With the forty-fold price,
follow the flow of the Hé and Jì rivers,
and transport it south to Liáng, Zhào, Sòng, Wèi, and Púyáng.
When a coarse diet lacks salt, the body swells;
the foundation of defending the frontiers
relies especially heavily on the use of salt.
If Your Lordship cuts firewood from the marshes
and boils the water of the Jǐ to levy taxes from the world,
then the wealth of the world will not decrease.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“I wish to enrich the foundation and make the five grains abundant, is that possible?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“It is not.
If the foundation is rich and goods are numerous, but you cannot protect them,
then they are taxed away by the world.
When the five grains flourish and are abundant,
if they are cheap for us while they are expensive for the world,
then they are taxed away by the world,
and then our people will always be captives of the world.
Those who are good at using the foundation
are like those who use a boat to cross the great sea,
observing from where the wind arises.
If the world’s prices are high, be high;
if the world’s prices are low, be low.
If the world is high while I am low,
then wealth and profits will be taxed away by the world.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“Is everything contained in this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Not yet.
Qí is a fundamental place where thoroughfares meet,
where goods are distributed and reach everywhere,
and it is the route for traveling scholars and merchants.
When people come to our land,
they eat our grain,
use our currency,
and only then do Qíjì horses and gold
go out. Issue orders with speed or delay
and make goods light or heavy;
then the treasures of the world will all be used by me.
The skillful use what they do not possess
and employ those who are not their own people.”
Qí Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“From the time of Suìrén onward,
may I hear about their great assemblies?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Since Suìrén, there have been none who did not use the principle of light and heavy to govern the world.
When Gònggōng was king,
water occupied seven-tenths of the area
and land occupied three-tenths;
he took advantage of the natural terrain to control the world through narrow passes.
By the time of Huángdì's kingship,
he was careful to escape the claws and teeth of beasts,
though his tools were not sharp.
He burned the mountains and forests,
broke through the thickets,
scorched the marshes,
and chased away the birds and beasts
to provide substance and benefit for the people;
only then could the world be shepherded.
By the time of Yáo and Shùn's kingship,
the means they used to transform the lands within the seas
were to use the jade of the Yúshì in the north
and to value the pearls of the Jiāng and Hàn in the south;
to overcome the birds and beasts,
they had the high officials follow suit.”
Huán Gōng asked:
“What does that mean?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“An order was issued: ‘The sons of feudal lords who wish to present tribute
must all use two tiger skins;
ministers and high officials must use leopard decorations,
and ranked officials must use leopard-skin aprons.’
The high officials distributed the grain of their cities
and their wealth
to buy tiger and leopard skins.
Therefore, the people of the mountains and forests hunted fierce beasts
as if they were pursuing an enemy of their kin.
Thus Your Lordship wears ceremonial robes at court,
while the fierce beasts are overcome outside.
The high officials have already distributed their wealth,
and the ten thousand people receive its flow.
This was the method of Yáo and Shùn.”
Huán Gōng said:
“‘Two names for affairs
and five names for standards
will bring order to the world,’
what is meant by ‘two names for affairs’?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“The celestial count
is Yáng,
and the terrestrial count
is Yīn;
these are called the ‘two names for affairs’.”
“What is meant by ‘five names for standards’?”
He replied:
“The weight, the balance, the compass, the square, and the water level;
these are called the ‘five names for standards.’
Regarding colors,
they are blue, yellow, white, black, and red.
Regarding sounds,
they are Gōng, Shāng, Yǔ, Zhǐ, and Jué.
Regarding flavors,
they are sour, pungent, salty, bitter, and sweet.
Regarding these ‘two and five,’
even with bare mountains and exhausted marshes,
the ruler uses calculations to control the people.
Flavors
are the means to control the mouths of the people;
sounds
are the means to control the ears of the people;
colors
are the means to control the eyes of the people.
A ruler who loses these ‘two and five’
will lose his state;
a high official who loses these ‘two and five’
will lose his power;
a commoner who loses these ‘two and five’
will lose his family.
This is the ultimate mechanism of the state,
called the mechanism of the state.”
The law of light and heavy says:
“If one claims to be able to serve as a Sīmǎ but cannot,
kill him to smear his blood on the drums;
if one claims to be able to manage the fields but cannot,
kill him to smear his blood on the altar of the soil;
if one claims to be able to serve as an official but cannot,
brand his face and make him a gatekeeper.”
Therefore, no one dares to fake ability or falsely claim a salary
from the ruler.
Thus the Prime Minister appoints people to official posts;
even those who cannot guard the gates or strike the watchman’s clapper
are also dealt with according to the law.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“I ask about losing the balance.”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Losing the balance means
the world controls me and I have no control over it.
This is called
losing the balance.”
Huán Gōng asked:
“What does that mean?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Suppose the world currently raises troops against us,
those ministers capable of planning to strengthen the state and stabilize the people
are granted land and titles;
those ministers capable of using chariot troops to advance and retreat to achieve success and fame
are granted land and titles.
In this way, it is the world that grants land to Your Lordship’s ministers,
not Your Lordship who grants it.
When the world has already caused ten lǐ to be granted to Your Lordship’s ministers,
every time the world moves,
it results in an additional twenty lǐ being granted to Your Lordship’s people.
It is not that Your Lordship’s people are rich;
neighboring states make them rich.
Every time neighboring states move,
they further enrich Your Lordship’s people;
the poor become poorer
and the rich become richer.
This is the logic of losing the balance.”
Huán Gōng said:
"What is meant by this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Now if the world were to raise troops against us,
the people would abandon their plows and hoes
to hold spears in the field;
thus, the state would be unable to farm.
This is not a heavenly disaster,
but a human disaster.
If the ruler issues orders in the morning and demands supplies by evening,
the people will treat their wealth
and their five grains
as enemies, loathing them and letting them go.
Merchants will receive them and store them in granaries;
thus, a portion of the state's wealth will be with the merchants.
When the army is disbanded
and the people return to their work,
all things will return to their high value.
The merchants will then release their wealth and goods,
while a smaller portion of the state's currency is stored with the merchants.
In such a case,
currency will be heavy by three parts,
and goods will be light by three parts.
The merchants trade within this three-part interval;
the wealth and goods of the state
will all end up with the merchants,
and the ruler will have no policy to deal with it.
The people will control one another,
and the ruler will have no influence over the matter.
This is what is meant by the loss of the standard for 'light and heavy'."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"The ruler of men holds the root,
so that the people cannot hold the branch;
the ruler of men holds the beginning,
so that the people cannot hold the end.
For those who are on the road,
tax them at the crossroads and passes;
for grain,
guard it during the spring and autumn;
for all other goods,
establish their value and let them circulate.
Thus, when goods move, respond to them.
Therefore, if you pre-emptively seize control of their routes,
the people will have nothing to follow;
if the ruler guards the flow,
the people will lose their high ground.
Thus, by guarding the high and low prices of the four directions,
the state will have no wandering merchants,
the expensive and cheap will be balanced,
and this is called the state's equilibrium.
By guarding one another through profit,
the calculations will then return to the ruler."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Those who are good at regulating the duties of merchants
will reduce the number of marketplaces;
reducing the number of marketplaces
will make the markets and courts leisurely;
when the markets and courts are leisurely,
the fields and wilderness will be filled;
when the fields and wilderness are filled,
the people's wealth will be sufficient.
When the people's wealth is sufficient,
the ruler's taxation will be inexhaustible.
Now it is not so:
when the people are heavy, the ruler is heavy,
and being heavy, he cannot make things light;
when the people are light, the ruler is light,
and being light, he cannot make things heavy.
The best rulers under heaven are not so:
when the people are heavy, the ruler is light;
when the people are light, the ruler is heavy.
This is the technique of using the surplus of wealth to fill the deficit.
Therefore, all those who cannot harmonize the people's profits
cannot achieve great order;
those who are not perceptive of the end and the beginning
cannot reach the pinnacle.
Moving those on the left and right by relying on one another's importance
is the policy of twenty states.
Salt and iron are the policy of twenty states.
Tin and gold are the policy of twenty states.
The calculations of the five officials
are not taxed from the people."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"Where do the calculations of light and heavy end?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Like the alternating succession of the four seasons,
they have no end.
When the state has troubles or worries,
use 'light and heavy' to adjust the five grains for use,
and accumulate surpluses and store excess to prepare for rewards.
When the world submits as guests
and you possess all within the seas,
use this to enrich the scholars of sincerity, trust, benevolence, and righteousness.
Thus, the people will value courtesy and yielding
and will not act in strange or eccentric ways.
As for those principles of 'light and heavy':
if the feudal lords do not submit,
use them to go to war;
if the feudal lords submit as guests,
use them to practice benevolence and righteousness."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"If one year of farming
provides five years of food,
the price of grain is fivefold.
If one year of farming
provides six years of food,
the price of grain is sixfold.
If two years of farming
provide eleven years of food,
then one who can take from the rich
and give to the poor
can then rule the world.
Furthermore, as for the world,
if one stays here and acts here,
in this way,
the world can be unified.
As for the world,
if you employ it without appearing to employ it,
and use it without appearing to use it.
Therefore, those who are good at governing the world
do not say they are employing it,
but make it so it must be employed;
they do not say they are using it,
but make it so it must be used."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Those who are good at governing a state
are like gold and stone balancing each other;
if the weight is equal, the gold tips.
Therefore, governing through power makes the situation heavy;
governing through the Way makes the situation lean.
Now, if grain is heavy in our state
and light in the world,
then the feudal lords' grain will naturally flow
like water from a source seeking lower ground.
Therefore, when goods are heavy, they arrive;
when they are light, they depart.
If there are goods that arrive because they are heavy
and remain even when light,
if I move and arrange them,
then the world will already belong to me.
When goods are stored, they become heavy;
when released, they become light;
when scattered, they become abundant.
When currency is heavy, the people will risk death for profit;
when currency is light, it is cast aside and not used.
Therefore, light and heavy are adjusted by calculations and then stopped."
"The five grains
are the masters of the people's lives.
Knife-money and currency
are like irrigation ditches.
Orders and commands
are like the speed of flow.
'Orders are more important than treasures, and the altars of earth and grain are more important than relatives.'
What does this mean?"
He replied:
"When the city walls are captured,
and the altars of earth and grain no longer receive blood sacrifices,
there are no living officials;
after parents pass away,
there are no sons who die for them.
This is why the altars of earth and grain are more important than relatives.
Therefore, to have people but no city walls
is called guarding a level emptiness;
to have people but no armor and weapons and no food
is called living with disaster."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"I have heard that there are seven policies regarding jade and currency within the four seas;
may I hear about them?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The ruǎngōng stone of Yīn Shān
is one policy;
the silver of Zǐ Shān in Yān
is one policy;"
The patterned skins of Fā and Cháoxiǎn
constitute one strategy;
the gold on the right thoroughfares of the Rǔ and Hànshuǐ
constitute one strategy;
the pearls of Jiāngyáng
constitute one strategy;
the malachite of Qínmíng Shān
constitutes one strategy;
the jade of the frontier mountains of Yúzhì
constitutes one strategy.
This is what is called taking a few to make many,
and taking the narrow to make the wide.
The calculations of the world
are all contained within the principles of "Light and Heavy."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"The horses of Yīn Shān
are enough to harness a thousand chariots.
The standard price of a horse is ten thousand,
and the standard price of gold is ten thousand.
I have a thousand catties of hidden gold;
how should I handle this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request that you command those responsible for the tax registers to have all taxes returned in gold instead of currency.
I will then reach forty thousand.
This makes one become four.
I did not mold clay or operate a furnace to create gold;
that the value of gold has now become four for every one is due to calculation.
Pearls originate from the faint light at the edge of Chìyě;
gold originates from the right thoroughfares of the Rǔ and Hànshuǐ;
jade originates from the frontier mountains of Yúzhì.
These are estimated to be seven thousand eight hundred li from Zhōu;
the route is far,
and the arrival is difficult.
Therefore, the former kings measured their value and followed this;
pearls and jade were made the upper currency,
gold was made the middle currency,
and knife-coins and cloth-money were made the lower currency.
The former kings raised or lowered the middle currency
to regulate the use of the lower and upper currencies.
For a state of one hundred chariots,
a market is established in the center,
and it measures fifty li to the east, west, south, and north.
In one day, the plan is determined;
on the second day, the loading is determined;
on the third day, it departs the border;
on the fifth day, it returns.
For the system of one hundred chariots
regarding 'Light and Heavy,' it should not exceed five days.
For a state of one hundred chariots, it plows
ten thousand qǐng of fields,
comprises ten thousand households,
has a population of one hundred thousand people,
has ten thousand people as workers,
has one hundred light chariots,
and four hundred horses.
For a state of one thousand chariots,
a market is established in the center,
and it measures over one hundred and fifty li to the east, west, south, and north.
On the second day, the plan is determined;
on the third day, the loading is determined;
on the fifth day, it departs the border;
on the tenth day, it returns.
For the system of one thousand chariots
regarding 'Light and Heavy,' it should not exceed one xún.
For a state of one thousand chariots, it plows
one hundred thousand qǐng of fields,
comprises one hundred thousand households,
has a population of one million people,
has one hundred thousand people as workers,
has one thousand light chariots,
and four thousand horses.
For a state of ten thousand chariots,
a market is established in the center,
and it measures five hundred li to the east, west, south, and north.
On the third day, the plan is determined;
on the fifth day, the loading is determined;
on the tenth day, it departs the border;
on the twentieth day, it returns.
For the system of ten thousand chariots
regarding 'Light and Heavy,' it should not exceed two xún.
For a state of ten thousand chariots, it plows
one million qǐng of fields,
comprises one million households,
has a population of ten million people,
has one million people as workers,
has ten thousand light chariots,
and forty thousand horses."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"A single man is a widower;
a single woman is a widow;
those who are old and without children are solitary.
If the ruler asks about those who had sons or brothers who died while serving as teachers or in labor corvée,
their parents are solitary,
and the superior must provide for their burial:
three sets of robes and shrouds,
and the coffin wood must be three inches thick;
the village officials manage the matter,
and they are buried in public land.
If a child is born without brothers,
the superior must bestow upon them a plot of land for a horse.
Therefore, parents will not feel it is a hardship
for their children to be used by the superior.
Throughout the year, the ruler travels through the towns and villages.
If people's strength is equal but their houses are beautiful,
they are good subjects,
those who labor diligently;
two bundles of dried meat
and one dàn of wine
shall be bestowed upon them.
For those whose strength is sufficient
but who wander idly and do not work,
the elderly shall reprimand them,
and those in their prime shall be sent to the border for garrison duty.
People who have no means of support shall be lent garden lands.
Thus all matters are undertaken,
and there are no people with idle strength or lost time.
These are all calculations of the state's strategies."
A superior farmer supports five people;
a middle farmer supports four;
a lower farmer supports three.
A superior woman produces five garments;
a middle woman four;
a lower woman three.
Farmers have their regular occupation,
and women have their regular work.
If one farmer does not plow,
someone will go hungry because of it;
if one woman does not weave,
someone will be cold because of it.
Hunger and freezing
must surely arise from the soil;
therefore, the former kings were careful at the beginning.
If work produces twice the basic requirement,
the people will not sell their children.
If it is three times the requirement,
it is enough for food.
If it is four times the requirement,
then the village will be sufficient.
If it is five times the requirement,
then the distant and near will communicate,
and then the dead can be buried.
If the work cannot reach twice the basic requirement,
yet the superior's demands are without end,
then the paths of wickedness
cannot be avoided by anyone,
and goods and wealth will not be secure even under restraint.
If one then pursues them with laws,
then it is to strike at the people from within.
When the 'Light and Heavy' is not adjusted,
people without even gruel cannot be held to principles,
and those who sell their children cannot be made to serve.
The ruler loses his people,
and the father loses his son;
this is the calculation for a fallen state.
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"The calculation of Shénnóng says:
'If one grain does not ripen,
reduce the demand for that one grain;
the rule for grain will make it tenfold in price.
If two grains do not ripen,
reduce the demand for those two grains;
the rule for grain will make it twenty times in price.'
Use coarse grain to fill the void;
give old grain to those without food,
and lend new seed to those without seed.
Thus there will be no tenfold prices,
and no people burdened by doubled weights of suffering."
Qí Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"May I hear about Guó Zhǔn?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"As for Guó Zhǔn,
it is to observe the times and establish norms."
Huán Gōng said:
"What is meant by 'observing the times and establishing norms'?"
He replied:
"When Huáng Dì was king,
he was careful to conceal his weapons.
When Yǒu Yú was king,
he bared the mountains and exhausted the marshes.
When the Xià Hòu were kings,
they burned the thickets and swamps,
set fire to the marshes,
but did not increase the people's profit.
When the Yīn people were kings,
the feudal lords had no enclosures for cattle and horses,
and they did not make their tools profitable.
When the Zhōu people were kings,
they employed capable officials to prepare materials.
The methods of these five houses were different, but their application was one."
Huán Gōng said:
"If that is so, among the methods of the five houses, which was the best?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Burning the mountain forests,
clearing the thickets and swamps,
and setting fire to the marshes
was because birds and beasts were numerous.
As for baring the mountains and exhausting the marshes,
it was because the ruler's wisdom was insufficient.
Burning the thickets and swamps,
setting fire to the marshes,
not increasing the people's profit,
concealing mechanical tools,
and closing off knowledge and capability
were to assist oneself.
That the feudal lords had no enclosures for cattle and horses
and did not make their tools profitable
was to avoid extravagant tools and to unify the people's hearts.
Using men to manage men,
avoiding spears and blades,
exalting benevolence and righteousness,
and riding upon the natural stability of Heaven
to secure oneself.
The methods of the five houses were different, but their application was one."
Huán Gōng said:
"For a ruler of the present age,
what should be established to be effective?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request that you use all five houses concurrently, but do not exhaust them."
Huán Gōng said:
"What do you mean?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Establish prayers for blessings to secure the mountains and marshes;
establish mechanical tools to make use of all things;
let the whole world benefit
while you carefully hold the heavy whip.
Bare the mountains and exhaust the marshes,
increase profit and gather the wealth.
Extract gold from the mountains to establish currency,
preserve the marshy hills,
and establish side-by-side enclosures
to provide abundance for the people.
Those swampy and overgrown lands
are not where the five grains grow;
they are the grounds for elk, deer, cattle, and horses.
Tax the newborn and cull the old in spring and autumn,
and establish distributions to protect the five grains;
this uses useless land to store the people's surplus.
The methods of the five houses
should all be used but not exhausted."
Huán Gōng said:
"The kings of the five generations
have already exhausted the methods of the world;
can I hear about the kings
of future generations?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Be fond of scrutiny without causing disorder,
change rapidly without being capricious;
act when the time arrives,
and stop when it has passed.
The methods of a King cannot be established in advance.
This is the Guó Zhǔn of the five houses."
Huán Gōng said:
"Is there a fixed calculation for Qīng Zhòng?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Qīng Zhòng has no fixed calculation.
When things happen, respond to them;
when sound is heard, ride upon it.
Therefore, if a state cannot attract the wealth of the world
and draw the people of the world,
then the state cannot be successful."
Huán Gōng said:
"What is meant by 'attracting the wealth of the world'?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"In the past, during the time of Jié,
there were thirty thousand female musicians;
their loud singing and morning music
were heard at the Sān Qú,
and there were none among them who did not wear embroidered robes.
Yī Yǐn used the traveling women of Bó
to work on embroidery and braiding;
for one roll of cloth, they obtained a hundred zhōng of grain in the state of Jié.
Now, the state of Jié
was the state of the Son of Heaven.
Jié had no worries about the world,
adorning himself with the music of women, bells, and drums;
thus Yī Yǐn was able to get his grain and divert his resources.
This is called 'attracting the wealth of the world'."
Huán Gōng said:
"What is meant by 'drawing the people of the world'?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request that every prefecture have an overseer,
and every village have five granary pits.
To those among the people who cannot pay their taxes,
give them long-term loans;
to those who die and are not buried,
give them long-term aid for the tomb.
When the hungry get food,
the cold get clothing,
the dead get burial,
and the destitute get relief,
then the way the world returns to me will be like flowing water.
This is called 'drawing the people of the world'.
Therefore, the Sage is good at using what is not his
and employing those who are not his own;
by moving words and swaying speech,
the ten thousand people can be befriended."
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"Tāng, with the seventy lǐ of Bó,
took over the world of Jié;
what was the reason?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Jié,
in winter did not build bridges
and in summer did not provide rafts,
so as to watch people freeze and drown.
He released tigresses into the marketplace
so as to watch the people's panic.
When it came to Tāng, it was not so.
At Yí and Shū, he stored grain;
he fed the hungry,
clothed the cold,
and relieved the destitute;
the world returned to Tāng like flowing water.
This is how Jié lost his empire."
Huán Gōng said:
"That Jié allowed Tāng to do this—
what was the reason?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Nǚ Huá
was beloved by Jié,
and Tāng served her with a thousand pieces of gold;
Qǔ Nì
was favored by Jié,
and Tāng served him with a thousand pieces of gold.
Internally there was the hidden influence of Nǚ Huá,
externally there was the overt influence of Qǔ Nì;
when the hidden and overt discussions agreed,
he was able to become the Son of Heaven.
This was the secret strategy of Tāng."
Huán Gōng said:
“The calculations of light and heavy,
and the standard distribution of the state,
I have already heard of them.
May I ask about the use of troops?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“There are five wars to be waged before reaching the use of weapons.”
Huán Gōng said:
“What do you mean by this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“I request to speak of the war of balance, the war of standards, the war of flow, the war of weights, and the war of strategic power.
This is what is meant by five wars before reaching the use of weapons.”
Huán Gōng said:
“Excellent.”
Huán Gōng wished to reward the descendants of those who died in service to the state.
He said:
“My state
is a land located at the crossroads,
a capital of food supplies,
and a place where tigers and wolves dwell.
Now, in every battle,
the dead are carried and the wounded are supported.
Regarding the orphans:
the grandchildren of the white-haired elderly,
who look up to the precious legacy of those who laid down their halberds,
I have no means to provide for them.
What should be done about this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“The powerful families of our state:
those who have moved to fiefs, live on incomes from their estates, and reside there,
if My Lord distinguishes them with certain goods,
then those goods become heavy.
If you do not distinguish them with those goods,
then the goods become light.
If you maintain control over them with goods,
then the goods become heavy.
If you do not maintain control with them,
then the goods become light.
Therefore, those with moved fiefs, those with incomes from estates,
wealthy merchants, hoarding traders,
and families with accumulated surpluses, stockpiled reserves, and hidden wealth—
these are the powerful of our state.
Therefore, let My Lord please wear plain white silk and go to the dwellings of the scholars.
Summon the meritorious officials, the noble families, those with fiefs and incomes, and the families with accumulated surpluses and stored reserves,
and say:
‘A fat city attracts battering rams;
lack of supplies leads to being besieged.
When the world is full of concerns,
shall Qí alone not participate in the planning?
You, Great Officers, who have the five grains, beans, and millet—
do not dare to speculate with them.
I request to purchase them from you at a fair price.’
Establish with them the notches on the contracts and tallies.
For the quantities in *fǔ* and *ōu*,
there must be no inflation or reduction.
When the destitute people
hear of this and go to buy grain,
the measuring by *fǔ* and *ōu* will not stop,
and trade from afar will not be rejected.
The price of the state’s grain
will naturally rise forty-fold.
Then My Lord can release the grain at forty times the price
to provide relief for the orphans and widows,
gather the poor and sick,
and look after the elderly who live alone,
are destitute, and have no children.
Do not let them be forced to sell themselves for support,
nor let them fall into the ditches and gutters.
If this is done,
then the soldiers will vie to be in the front ranks of battle,
and they will serve without being lazy.
They will carry the dead and support the wounded,
and more than half would be willing to die.
What is the reason for this?
It is not that the soldiers love war or value death lightly;
it is the distribution of light and heavy that makes it so.”
Huán Gōng said:
“The taxes on hides, tree trunks, tendons, and horns are very heavy.
To levy heavy taxes on the people
and then have the market sell
hides, trunks, tendons, and horns at high prices
is not the method for governing the state.”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“I request that you order the raising of steep embankments and the blocking of ponds with thorns,
so that East and West cannot see each other,
and North and South cannot see each other.”
Huán Gōng said:
“Agreed.”
After this was carried out for one year,
the taxes on hides, trunks, tendons, and horns were reduced by half,
and the levies on the people were reduced by half.
Huán Gōng summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
“What is the reason for this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“When the embankments and ponds were level,
husband and wife could pull a cart
and easily cover a hundred *lǐ*.
Now with steep embankments and thorny ponds,
East, West, North, and South cannot see one another.
When the heavens pour down heavy rain,
the strength of ten men cannot pull a cart up.
In the broad marshes when encountering rain,
the strength of ten men cannot be relied upon.
Thus there is no way to utilize the strength of cattle and horses.
The cattle and horses become exhausted and die one after another where they stand, their bodies visible everywhere.
Hides, trunks, tendons, and horns
are given to people for nothing, yet no one takes them.
The price of cattle and horses
will naturally rise a hundred-fold.
When the world hears of this,
they will bring their cattle and horses
and flock to Qí like a flowing stream.
Therefore, steep embankments and thorny ponds
are the means to attract the world’s cattle and horses
and to reduce the levies on our people.
The *Dào Ruò Mì* says:
‘That which is produced
is not as much as that which is gathered.’ ”
Huán Gōng said:
“Among the bows and crossbows, many are warped and bent.
Although I levy heavy taxes on the people
to support the repair craftsmen, yet the bows and crossbows remain mostly warped and bent.
What is the reason for this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Geese and ducks stay in nearby dwellings,
but the flight of the *kūn jī*, swans, and *hú qiú* is far-reaching.
Wherever the swans and *kūn* birds are,
I request that My Lord present jade disks to invite hunters.”
Huán Gōng said:
“Agreed.”
After this was carried out for one year,
there were no deficiencies among the superiors,
and no deserters in the front ranks.
Within three months, the quivers were opened,
and there were no warped bows or crossbows.
He summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
“What is the reason for this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Wherever the swans and *kūn* birds were,
My Lord presented jade disks to invite hunters.
When the people of the marshes heard of this,
they crossed the plains to shoot at long range.
Without a crossbow of ten *jūn* strength,
one cannot hit the *kūn jī*, swan, or *hú qiú*.
Those crossbows of ten *jūn* strength,
without the use of corrective frames and presses,
cannot straighten themselves.
Therefore, within three months the quivers were opened
and there were no warped bows or crossbows.
Why is this?
It is because each household practiced with their equipment in their own place.”
Huán Gōng said:
“I wish to levy a tax on houses.”
Guǎn Zǐ replied: “You cannot;
this is to destroy what has been completed.”
“I wish to levy a tax on the ten thousand people.”
Guǎn Zǐ said:
“You cannot;
this is to suppress the people’s feelings.”
“I wish to levy a tax on the six domestic animals.”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“You cannot;
this is to kill the living.”
“I wish to levy a tax on trees.”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“You cannot;
this is to cut down life.”
“In that case, upon what may I levy a tax?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“I request that My Lord levy a tax upon the ghosts and spirits.”
Huán Gōng suddenly changed his expression and said:
"If the ten thousand people, the houses,
the six domestic animals, and the trees
cannot yet be taxed,
can ghosts and spirits then be taxed?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Satisfaction should follow what is appropriate; power
is gained through the advantage of circumstances;
deliberation depends on authority,
and the scope of affairs is vast.
A king relies on power,
a sage relies on subtlety,
and both harmonize with all things."
Huán Gōng said:
"How should we proceed?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"In the past, the Wǔ Gēng and
Five Officials of Yáo had nothing to eat.
I ask the Ruler to establish sacrifices to the Wǔ Lì,
to sacrifice to the five officials of Yáo.
In spring, offer orchids;
in autumn, gather fallen leaves;
use river fish as dried jerky,
and use salamanders as appetizers.
If this is done,
then the taxes on marsh fish
will be a hundred times more than in the past,
and there will be no need for taxes on houses, grain, or national cloth.
This is what is called establishing it through prayers for auspiciousness
and promoting it through ritual and righteousness.
Thus, you will be self-sufficient;
why seek anything from the people?"
Huán Gōng said: "Among the states of the world,
none is stronger than Yuè.
Now I wish to take military action in the north against Gūzhú and Lízhi,
but I fear the arrival of the Yuè people.
Is there a way to deal with this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I ask the Ruler to dam the source of the streams,
let the high officials build ponds,
and order that swimming in formation be their pleasure.
Then how would the Yuè people dare to come?"
Huán Gōng said:
"How should we proceed?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I ask to issue an order to control the three rivers,
establish the capital of Yuán,
and establish the capital of Large Boats.
At the capital of Large Boats
there are deep abysses with embankments ten fathoms high.
Issue an order saying:
'Those who can swim will be rewarded with ten pieces of gold.'
Before even a thousand pieces of gold are spent,
the swimming skills of the people of Qí
will not yield to those of Wú or Yuè."
Huán Gōng eventually took military action in the north against Gūzhú and Lízhi.
The Yuè people indeed arrived,
but they were stopped at Qūzī by the water control of Qí.
Guǎn Zǐ had fifty thousand soldiers trained in swimming
waiting
to battle at Qūzī,
and they greatly defeated the Yuè people.
This is what is called 'Water Preparedness.'
The northern marshes of Qí caught fire, and the fire's
light illuminated the hall.
Guǎn Zǐ entered to congratulate Huán Gōng, saying:
"Our fields are cleared,
and the farmers will surely have a hundredfold profit."
That year, the taxes were fully collected by the ninth month,
and the grain was of fine quality.
Huán Gōng summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied: "A state of ten thousand chariots
or a state of a thousand chariots
cannot cook without firewood.
Now that the northern marshes have burned and no one can replant them,
the farmers can stay at home
and sell their brushwood and kindling,
with one bundle worth ten times its usual price.
Thus in spring they have the means to use their plows,
and in summer they have the means to do their weeding.
This is why the taxes were fully collected by the ninth month."
Huán Gōng was worried about the poverty of the people in the northern suburbs
and summoned Guǎn Zǐ to ask:
"In the northern suburbs,
the people are all makers of hemp sandals and thread,
who rely on orchards for their basic profit.
Is there a way to help them?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I ask to issue an order: families with a hundred zhōng of grain are forbidden from making hemp sandals,
families with a thousand zhōng are forbidden from maintaining orchards,
and those living within three hundred paces of the market are forbidden from planting mallows or vegetables.
If this is done,
then the vacant fields will provide resources for each other,
and the commoners of the northern suburbs
will have a market for their products. Their manual labor
and the profits from their orchards
will therefore be ten times greater."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"There are three states that are hidden kings,
and Qí is among them."
Huán Gōng said:
"Can I hear about these words?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Chǔ has the gold of the Rǔ and Hàn rivers,
Qí has the salt of Qūzhǎn,
and Yān has the salt-boiling of Liáodōng;
these are the states of hidden kings.
Moreover, Chǔ having gold
is like Qí having raw whetstones.
If it is not handled skillfully
or used well,
the world will look askance at them.
If I, Yíwú, were allowed to manage the gold of Chǔ,
I could make it so that farmers do not have to plow yet have food,
and women do not have to weave yet have clothes.
Now Qí has the salt of Qūzhǎn;
I ask the Ruler to have marsh firewood cut
to boil the marsh water into salt,
and then officially store it."
Huán Gōng said:
"Very well."
The official collection began in the tenth month,
and by the first month,
thirty-six thousand zhōng of salt were produced.
He summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
"How should we use this salt?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"When the first month of spring arrives,
agricultural work will begin.
The high officials should not be allowed to repair tombs,
renovate palaces,
build terraces,
or construct walls.
The masses of the northern sea
should not be allowed to gather labor to boil salt.
If this is done,
the price of salt will naturally rise tenfold."
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent.
How should we proceed?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I ask to issue an order to sell it to Liáng, Zhào, Sòng, Wèi, and Pǔyáng.
Those countries must provide food for their people.
Without salt, they will suffer from swelling;
states that guard their borders
use salt in particularly great quantities."
Huán Gōng said:
"Very well."
He then issued the order to sell it
and obtained over eleven thousand jīn of gold.
Huán Gōng summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
"How should we use the gold?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I ask to issue an order that congratulatory offerings
and those paying regular taxes must use gold.
The price of gold will naturally rise a hundredfold.
Using the weight of gold as a balance
to measure all things, all will return to the Ruler.
Therefore, this is what is called using resources
as if drawing from the Yellow River or the sea,
or as if providing for a team of horses.
This is the enterprise of a hidden king."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"A state of ten thousand chariots
must have merchants worth ten thousand pieces of gold;
a state of one thousand chariots
must have merchants worth one thousand pieces of gold;
a state of one hundred chariots
must have merchants worth one hundred pieces of gold.
They are not what the ruler relies upon;
they are those with whom the ruler competes.
Therefore, if a ruler of men does not carefully examine his commands and decrees,
then within a single state there will be two rulers and two kings."
Huán Gōng said:
"What is meant by 'one state having two rulers and two kings'?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Now, when your lordship's taxes and levies
are collected correctly, yet the prices of all goods
drop and lose their proper share,
they all flow into the hands of the merchants.
This is having two rulers and two kings within one state.
Therefore, merchants exploit these hardships to watch for the people's needs;
the poor lose their wealth,
which is a doubling of their poverty;
the farmers lose their five grains,
which is a doubling of their exhaustion.
Therefore, if a ruler of men cannot carefully guard his mountains and forests,
marshes and wetlands, and brushlands,
he cannot be established as a king of the world."
Huán Gōng said:
"What do these words mean?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Mountains, forests, marshes, wetlands, and brushlands
are where firewood and fuel are produced,
and where sacrificial animals are raised.
Therefore, have the people seek them,
have the people register them,
and use them to supply their needs.
When the ruler shows private affection for the people,
it is like a younger brother to an elder brother,
or a son to a father;
only then can wealth be circulated and loans exchanged.
Therefore, I request to take your lordship's idle wealth
and distribute it throughout the towns and villages.
In the bright spring, when the time for silkworms and mulberries is about to arrive,
I request to provide them with food and the necessary baskets and frames for silkworm rearing.
In this way,
the taxes on raw silk will be collected in full as they are gathered.
Furthermore, lest the people from the four quarters fail to arrive,
manage them according to the six seasons:
Spring is called 'planting the plowshares,'
next is 'harvesting wheat,'
next is 'weeding the hemp,'
next is 'planting hemp,'
next is 'cutting from the marshes,'
and next is 'the great rains are about to arrive,'
quickly weed and hill up the soil.
Manage these according to the six seasons
to provide supplies even to the state capital.
One who is good at this follows the relative value of goods in the townships,
guards the granaries and storehouses,
and thus affairs are handled without error as they arise.
Only then can one be established as a king of the world."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"If one farmer does not plow,
someone among the people may go hungry;
if one woman does not weave,
someone among the people may be cold.
Therefore, if the output of labor is double the basic requirement,
there will be no one who sells their children;
if the output is triple the basic requirement,
then food and clothing will be sufficient;
if the output is quadruple the basic requirement,
then official taxes can be supplied;
if the output is quintuple the basic requirement,
then the far and near will be connected,
and the dead can be buried.
Now, if labor cannot double the basic requirement,
yet the demands of the superiors have no end,
this makes it so that dangerous paths cannot be traveled alone,
and lost goods cannot be left alone.
If you follow this with laws,
it is like mowing down the people.
If people eat three shēng,
then the township will have those lacking food who turn to theft;
if they eat two shēng,
then the village will have those lacking food who turn to theft;
if they eat one shēng,
then the household will have those lacking food who turn to theft.
Now, while employing unsustainable methods,
yet consuming grain at forty times its cost,
to demand that the people do not lose their way
is impossible.
Furthermore, when the ruler issues an order in the morning and demands its completion by evening,
those who have property bring out their wealth,
those who have nothing sell their clothes and shoes,
and farmers sell their five grains
at one-third the price and leave.
Thus, a single outburst of anger from the ruler's morning order
causes cloth and silk to flow out to the rest of the world.
When the ruler's demands have no end,
and the people have no way to meet them,
they flee and take refuge in mountains and hills.
Soldiers holding spears
look back and feel no kinship;
families are lost and not unified.
With the people fleeing within
and the scholars escaping to the outside,
this is an internal collapse without even waiting for battle."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Now, for those who possess land and shepherd the people for the state,
the priority lies in the four seasons,
and the defense lies in the granaries.
When the state has much wealth,
those from afar will come;
when the land is reclaimed and cultivated,
the people will remain and dwell;
when the granaries are full,
they will know ritual and propriety;
when food and clothing are sufficient,
they will know honor and shame.
Now, even if your lordship personally plows the fields,
breaking the grass and soil,
and obtains the grain; and for the people's food,
each person has a certain number of paces and acres,
yet there are still those starving in the streets and alleys—why is this?
It is because the grain has been hoarded.
Now, your lordship casts coins and establishes currency
for the people to circulate,
and each person has a hundred or ten of them,
yet there are still people who sell their children—why is this?
It is because wealth has been monopolized.
Therefore, if a ruler of men cannot disperse the accumulations,
regulate high and low prices,
and redistribute monopolized wealth,
then even if the ruler strengthens the foundation and urges plowing,
breaking grass and establishing currency without end,
the people will still be insufficient."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ, saying:
"Now I wish to regulate high and low prices,
redistribute monopolized wealth,
and disperse the accumulations.
Otherwise,
the world will engage in mergers and acquisitions without end,
storing up surpluses and hoarding excesses without ceasing,
while the poor, the lowly, the widowed, the orphaned, and the elderly will not share in it.
Is there a way to disperse them,
and a method for redistribution?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Only the masters of light and heavy can disperse them.
I request to command the masters of light and heavy."
Huán Gōng said:
"Very well."
He prepared five chariots
to welcome Guǐ Yǐ at Zhōu Xià Yuán.
Huán Gōng then
sat with Guǐ Yǐ, Guǎn Zǐ, and Nìng Qī in a group of four.
Huán Gōng said:
"I request to ask about the methods of light and heavy."
Guǐ Yǐ said:
"One who taxes his people heavily loses his subordinates;
one who frequently deceives the feudal lords has no authoritative allies."
Guǎn Zǐ leaned forward and asked:
"If I do not tax my people,
how shall I provide for chariots and armor?
If I do not tax my people,
how shall I deal with neighboring states?"
Guǐ Yǐ said:
“Only the ‘good heart’ is feasible!
When the heart is good, then all things circulate;
when all things circulate, then all things move;
when all things move, then all things become inexpensive;
when all things are inexpensive, then all things can be utilized.
One who knows all things can be utilized but does not utilize them
will be deprived by the world.
One who is deprived by the world
is a great thief of the state.”
Huán Gōng said:
“May I ask about the ‘good heart’ through which all things can be utilized?”
Guǐ Yǐ said:
“For those who have surplus wealth but no surplus carriages,
demand it from the Qīng and Zhūhóu.
For those who have sufficient means in their locale
but do not reward travelers,
demand it from the Lìng Dàfū.
If it is like this,
then all things will circulate;
when all things circulate,
then all things move;
when all things move,
then all things become inexpensive;
when all things are inexpensive,
then all things can be utilized.
Therefore, one who knows that the ‘three standards’ are the same plan
can manage the world;
one who does not know the ‘three standards’ are the same plan
cannot manage the world.
Thus, by extending orders
and regulating the pace of speed and slowness,
the people will return to me like flowing water.
This is the technique of ‘light and heavy.’”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“Now with a hundred thousand halberds deployed,
the consumption of firewood and vegetables
daily empties ten lǐ of fertile plains;
with one shout and the thrust of a halberd,
the expenditure of currency
daily depletes a thousand pieces of gold.
Over time, how shall we prepare for this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“If the price of grain is stable at forty per fǔ,
the price of gold is four thousand.
If grain is forty per fǔ,
then a zhōng is four hundred;
ten zhōng are four thousand;
twenty zhōng are eight thousand.
If the price of gold is four thousand,
then two pieces of gold equal eight thousand.
Thus, the work of one farmer
who plows a hundred mǔ for the whole year,
the harvest of a hundred mǔ
is no more than twenty zhōng;
the work of one farmer
is only equal to two pieces of gold in wealth.
Therefore, grain is heavy and gold is light,
or gold is heavy and grain is light;
the two do not stand in balance.
Therefore, the skillful ruler raises the price of grain.
If a fǔ is four hundred,
then a zhōng is four thousand;
ten zhōng are forty thousand;
twenty zhōng are eighty thousand.
If the price of gold is four thousand,
then ten pieces of gold are forty thousand;
twenty pieces of gold equal eighty thousand.
Thus, when issuing orders, say
that the work of one farmer
has the value of twenty pieces of gold.
In that case, land does not have width or narrowness
and the state does not have poverty or wealth;
it depends on being proficient in issuing orders
and being careful with the technique of ‘light and heavy.’”
Guǎn Zǐ said:
“With a thundering sound the drums are struck,
and the soldiers are filled with indignation;
with a clanging sound the gongs are struck,
and the soldiers move in unison.
When the drumsticks and drums are followed,
they carry the dead and assist the wounded,
striving to advance without stopping.
Their mouths are full of food,
their hands are full of money;
it is not because of a feud of their grandparents,
but because they are driven by heavy stipends and heavy rewards.
Therefore, when the carriages and crowns stand at court,
if rank and stipend do not follow,
the ministers will not be loyal;
when the central army goes to battle,
if the promised rewards do not follow,
the soldiers will not die in their ranks.
Thus, high ministers are held at court by their positions,
and the soldiers in the ranks are held by rewards.
Thus, to make a father unable to treat his son as a son,
a brother unable to treat his younger brother as a brother,
and a wife unable to have her husband—
only heavy stipends and heavy rewards can make it so.
Therefore, without considering the distance of the road,
one can overawe the people of distant regions;
without considering the danger of mountains and rivers,
one can subdue states that rely on their natural defenses;
erupting like thunder and lightning,
moving like wind and rain,
coming out and going in alone,
none can resist.”
Huán Gōng said:
“The barbarians of the four directions are not submissive;
I fear they may resist my governance
and travel throughout the world
to harm me.
Is there
a way for me to handle this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“If Wú and Yuè do not come to court,
shall we use pearls and ivory as currency?
If Fà and Cháoxiǎn do not come to court,
please request patterned skins and down
clothing to be used as currency.
If Yúshì does not come to court,
please use white jade disks as currency.
If the heights of Kūnlún do not come to court,
please use qiú, lín, and lánggān as currency.
For something that can be held in the hand without being seen,
held in the mouth without being seen,
yet is worth a thousand gold pieces—
that is a pearl;
after this, the Wú and Yuè of eight thousand lǐ away can be made to come to court.
A single leopard skin worth a thousand gold pieces;
after this,
the Fà and Cháoxiǎn of eight thousand lǐ away can be made to come to court.
For something that can be held in the bosom without being seen,
tucked under the arm without being seen,
yet is worth a thousand gold pieces—
that is a white jade disk;
after this, the Yúshì of eight thousand lǐ away can be made to come to court.
For hairpins and earrings worth a thousand gold pieces—
those are qiú, lín, and lánggān;
after this, the heights of Kūnlún of eight thousand lǐ away can be made to come to court.
Therefore, if goods have no master,
affairs have no connection,
and there is no way for the far and near to rely on each other,
then the barbarians of the four directions will not come to court.”
Huán Gōng asked:
“Can the morning and evening of the world be settled?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“It cannot be settled in a lifetime.”
Huán Gōng asked:
“May I hear the explanation for why it cannot be settled?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“The earth is twenty-eight thousand lǐ from east to west,
and twenty-six thousand lǐ from north to south.
The Son of Heaven stands in the center;
of the four sides of the state,
each side is over ten thousand lǐ.
The people who enter the formal tax registers
also span over ten thousand lǐ.
Thus, there are those with a hundredfold strength who do not arrive,
those with tenfold strength who do not arrive,
and those who are on the verge.
Then those who are far away become estranged and harbor resentment against the ruler.
