The border lords receive the ruler’s resentful people,
treat them well,
and then fail to come to court.
This is because the Son of Heaven blocks their path.
If those who ripen the grain leave,
how can the world be brought to hegemony?”
Huángōng asked:
"How should the affairs be carried out?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request to establish a hierarchy of territories
alongside the world.
The Tiānzǐ stands in the center,
with a territory of a thousand lǐ square.
The territory for concurrently hegemonizing should be over three hundred lǐ.
Lesser Zhūhóu are measured at one hundred lǐ.
Those near the sea of Zǐ or Nán rank are measured at seventy lǐ.
If it is like this,
then it is like the chest commanding the arm,
and the arm commanding the fingers.
Thus,
even if small portions cannot be divided among the people,
by adjusting according to supply and demand
and managing surpluses and deficiencies,
although they are below, they will not cause worry for the ruler.
The sea produces salt without stopping;
the mountains produce gold and timber without ceasing.
Grasses and trees grow according to the seasons;
implements wear out and currency circulates according to time;
the salt of the Jǐ River dissolves day by day.
When things end, they start again;
competing with heaven and earth—
this is called establishing the hierarchy of territories."
Wǔwáng asked Guǐdù:
"If ceremonial gifts are not heavy,
one's person is not close to the ruler;
if those on the left and right do not have enough,
friends and associates will not be well-regarded by the various ministers.
Therefore, I do not wish to collect taxes from households
yet provide for the needs of those on the left and right.
Is there a way for this?"
Guǐdù replied:
"Our state is a state situated at crossroads,
where remote grains are traded,
where traveling guests and merchants pass through,
and where goods and wealth converge.
Therefore, if they eat the grain of our state
and use the currency of our state,
only then will they carry gold and depart.
Thus, I ask the ruler to weight the heavy as heavy and balance the light as light,
managing goods to follow one another,
then the state policy can be accomplished.
Therefore, be careful not to lose the standard.
If it has not been given,
can the people be governed?"
Wǔwáng said:
"How should the affairs be carried out?"
Guǐdù said:
"Gold comes from the mountains on the right thoroughfare of the Rǔ and Hàn rivers;
pearls come from the faint light at the end of Chìyě;
jade comes from the mountains beside the Yúshì tribe.
These are all seven thousand eight hundred odd lǐ away from Zhōu.
The roads are long,
and the arrival is difficult.
Thus, the former kings measured their use by its weightiness,
consequently making pearls and jade the highest currency,
gold the middle currency,
and knives and cloth the lowest currency.
Thus, the former kings were skilled at managing high, low, and middle currencies
to regulate the use of lower and upper goods,
and thus the world was sufficient."
Huángōng said:
"Héng said to me:
'For one farmer's work,
they must have one plowshare, one weeding hoe, one sickle, one hoe, one mallet, and one reaping hook;
only then are they established as a farmer.
For one cart, there must be one axe, one saw, one axle-cap, one drill, one chisel, one mallet, and one spoke-shave;
only then is it established as a cart.
One woman must have one knife, one awl, one needle, and one large needle;
only then is she established as a woman.
I request an order to cut mountain timber
and smelt mountain iron;
this way we can have sufficient use without taxation.'"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"That is not possible.
Now, if you dispatch laborers and slaves to do it,
they will flee and not remain.
If you dispatch the common people,
then those below will harbor resentment against those above.
If there is war at the borders,
they will harbor deep-seated grudges and not fight.
Before the benefits of mountain iron are seen,
internal collapse will occur.
Therefore, those who are skilled at it find it better to give it to the people:
measure its weight,
calculate its profit,
the people get seven parts,
and the ruler gets three parts.
Mix this with the technique of light and heavy,
and manage it by high and low prices.
In this way,
the people will work diligently as if they were slaves for the ruler."
Huángōng said:
"I ask about the methods of the land."
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The Zhūhóu of the river banks
are states with a zhōng of grain per mǔ.
The Zhūhóu of the stony mountains are another kind of state.
The reason why the Zhūhóu of the river banks often cannot overcome the states of the mountain Zhūhóu
is because of preparedness."
Huángōng asked:
"What does this mean?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Now, the Zhūhóu of the river banks
are states with a zhōng of grain per mǔ;
therefore, grain is abundant
but not managed,
so they cannot keep it.
As for the states of the mountain Zhūhóu,
they collect greens and store vegetables;
this is what is meant by preparedness."
Huángōng said:
"Do the methods of the land end here?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Not yet.
Formerly, the Dí Zhūhóu
were a state with a zhōng per mǔ,
so ten zhōng of grain was worth a zī of gold.
The Chéng Zhūhóu
were a state of mountain Zhūhóu,
so five fǔ of grain was worth a zī of gold.
Thus, the Dí Zhūhóu, despite ten zhōng, could not afford to mount halberds,
while the Chéng Zhūhóu, with five fǔ, could mount halberds.
Ten times more yet insufficient,
or one-fifth yet having a surplus—
this is through understanding the methods of light and heavy, high and low.
If a state has ten years' worth of reserves
yet the people have insufficient food,
it is because they all look to the ruler's salary through their various occupations.
If the ruler has the wealth of mountains and seas
yet the people's needs are insufficient,
it is because they all exchange their various occupations with those above.
Therefore, rent and grain taxes are what the ruler should rightfully obtain;
direct labor taxes are what the ruler forcibly demands.
A ruler who loses his state abandons what he should rightfully obtain
and collects what he forcibly demands;
thus those below resent those above, and orders are not carried out.
When you take from the people, they are angry;
when you give to them, they are happy—
such is human nature.
The former kings knew this,
and so they showed the form of giving
but did not show the principle of taking.
Thus, the coming of the five grains and millet
is the people's arbiter of life;
gold, knives, and cloth
are the people's circulating currency.
The former kings were skilled at regulating the circulating currency
to control the arbiter of life;
thus the people's labor could be fully utilized."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"When spring rains reach five feet,
the ruler will surely be disgraced.
A state that measures its food will surely perish.
Many people wait for the five grains.
Thus, trees that withstand frost and dew
do not receive orders from Heaven;
families that are self-sufficient
do not follow a sage.
Therefore, take and then give,
raise and then lower,
anger and then please—
and the whole world can be mobilized."
Huán Gōng asked:
"By strengthening the foundation and being frugal with expenditures,
can one ensure survival?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"These can bring improvement and betterment,
but they are not sufficient to ensure survival.
Long ago, in the state of the Jì clan,
they strengthened the foundation and were frugal with expenditures.
Their five grains were abundant and overflowing,
but they could not manage them properly,
and they flowed out in all directions to the rest of the world.
If things are like this,
then the Jì clan's strengthening of the foundation and frugality
were just enough to cause their people
to exhaust their grain and, being unable to manage it, become captives of the world.
Because of this, their state perished
and they themselves had nowhere to stay.
Therefore, these can bring improvement
but are not sufficient for survival.
Thus, one who is good at governing a state ensures that
while the world is low,
I am high;
while the world is light,
I am heavy;
while the world has plenty,
I have little.
Only then can one receive the courtly homage of the world."
Huán Gōng said:
"I wish not to kill a single soldier
nor blunt a single halberd, yet open up two regional capitals.
Is there a way to do this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The upper and lower reaches of the Jīng Shuǐ are empty,
while the Wèn, Sì, Zhū, and Yán are three times full.
I request to issue an order to plant wheat in the ninth month
and harvest it when the summer solstice arrives,
so that the seasonal rains will not have fallen yet and the agricultural work will be benefited."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
He ordered the planting of wheat in the ninth month
and its harvest at the summer solstice.
Measuring the crop,
the accumulation of a single harvest
was equal to two regional capitals.
Therefore, this is what is called being good at following the seasons of heaven,
being discerning about the advantages of the earth,
and the way to open up regional capitals.
Guǎn Zǐ entered and reported back to Huán Gōng, saying:
"The annual land tax is forty-two thousand pieces of gold.
I request to use it for a morning of unconditional rewards for the soldiers."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
By order, a time was set to beat the drums at the wilds of Tàizhōu to assemble the soldiers.
Huán Gōng then ascended the altar and stood there.
Nìng Qī, Bǎo Shū, Xí Péng, Yì Yá, and Bīn Xūwú all stood shoulder to shoulder.
Guǎn Zǐ held the drumsticks, bowed to the soldiers, and said:
"Whoever can break through enemy formations and crush the masses,
will be granted one hundred pieces of gold."
He asked three times, but no one responded.
One man holding a sword came forward
and asked:
"How many people are in the 'masses'?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"A mass of one thousand people."
"A mass of one thousand people,
I can break through."
He was granted one hundred pieces of gold.
Guǎn Zǐ spoke again:
"When weapons engage and crossbows are drawn,
whoever can capture a company commander,
will be granted one hundred pieces of gold."
A man asked:
"How many people does the commander lead?"
Guǎn Zǐ said: "A commander of one thousand men."
"A commander of one thousand men,
I can capture him."
He was granted one hundred pieces of gold.
Guǎn Zǐ spoke again:
"Whoever can follow where the banners point
and capture the head of the enemy general,
will be granted one thousand pieces of gold."
Ten men lined up saying they could do it,
and each was granted one thousand pieces of gold.
Others who said they could behead enemies in the field
were each granted ten pieces of gold.
In a single morning of unconditional rewards, the forty-two thousand pieces of gold
were completely emptied.
Huán Gōng was startled and sighed deeply, saying:
"How shall I realize the benefit of this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"My Lord, do not worry.
This allows them to gain a reputation in their villages abroad,
achieve merit for their kinsmen at home,
and show virtue to their wives and children within the family.
In this way,
the soldiers will certainly compete for fame and repay your virtue;
they will have no thought of retreating.
When we raise troops and attack,
crushing their army
and annexing their land,
the profit will be far more than just forty-two thousand pieces of gold."
The five officials said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
Then he cautioned the great generals, saying:
"For a commander of one hundred men,
you must perform the courtly rites for him.
For a commander of one thousand men,
you must bow as you see him off,
descending two steps from your position.
For those with parents,
you must send them four dǎn of wine and
four cauldrons of meat.
For those without parents,
you must send their wives and children three dǎn of wine and
three cauldrons of meat."
This instruction was carried out for half a year;
fathers taught their sons,
elder brothers taught their younger brothers, and
wives exhorted their husbands,
saying:
"Seeing that he treats us with such generosity,
if you do not die in the ranks,
how could you face returning to the village?"
Huán Gōng then finally raised troops to attack Lái,
and they fought at Jǔbìshìlǐ.
Before the drums and banners were even in sight of each other,
and before the size of the forces was known,
the people of Lái fled in great numbers.
Consequently, they crushed their army,
annexed their territory,
and captured their general.
Thus, without distributing land for enfeoffment
or giving out gold as a reward,
the army of Lái was crushed,
its territory annexed,
and its ruler captured.
This was the strategy of unconditional rewards.
Huán Gōng said:
"In the battle of Qūfáng,
many people borrowed money to provide for the state's affairs.
I wish to give them compensation for this;
how should I go about it?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request that you issue an order:
order wealthy merchants and hoarders to provide one horse for every hundred tallies they hold;
those who have none
may obtain them from the state.
In this way,
the price of horses will certainly rise naturally to a hundred times the original cost.
Thus, the state's horses will not even leave their stables,
and the compensation for the battle of Qūfáng will be sufficient."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"The achievements of Chóngdì, Jiǎngdì, Dīng, and Huì have lasted for generations,
but I gain no net benefit from them annually.
I cannot collect even a peck or a pint of tax from them;
they are exempt.
As for the overgrown fields of Lái, salty lands, marshes,
and the unused soil among the mountain ramparts,
I cannot collect even a peck or a pint of tax from them;
they are exempt."
Row after row of crops border the fief for fifteen *lǐ*,
yet through forced farming they consider themselves self-sufficient.
Among those people, I, the lonely one, cannot tax even a *dǒu* or a *shēng*,
so I discard that one part.
Thus, of my state, I cannot control two-fifths.
This is having the title of a state of ten thousand chariots but the practical use of not even one thousand.
To balance the scales with the Son of Heaven
and contend for rank among the feudal lords,
is there a way to do this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Only by taxing through commands and orders can it be done."
Huán Gōng said:
"How is this carried out?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request an order to dispatch troops to establish garrisons and register the farmers.
Households with ten *zhōng* of grain shall not go,
households with one hundred *zhōng* shall not go,
households with one thousand *zhōng* shall not go.
Of those who go, there will not be one in a hundred,
or ten in a thousand,
yet the quantities in their granaries and pits
will all be revealed to the superiors.
Your Highness should examine the quantities in the granaries and pits and issue an order saying:
'The state is poor and its resources are insufficient;
I request to take grain from you at a fair price.'
Examine all the granaries and pits so that they cannot be hidden or reduced.
Your Highness should adjust the value of the currency
to determine the quantity
and ensure there are no debts or contracts involved.
Then the grain stored in granaries and pits will all return to Your Highness.
Thus, you will be peerless within the Jiǔzhōu,
and have no worries on your borders."
The Duke said:
"Dismiss the troops and return them to farming;
there is no use for them."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"If the world has war,
the stored grain will be sufficient to provide for rations.
If the world has no war,
then distribute it to the poor commoners.
In this way,
the marshlands, salt flats, alkaline wastes,
and the soil between the mountains and ramparts will all be cleared of weeds and cultivated.
This is called taxing through commands and orders."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"If the price of a *fǔ* of grain in Téng or Lǔ is one hundred,
then make the price of a *fǔ* of grain in our state one thousand.
The grain from Téng and Lǔ will flow from all sides and return to us,
like water flowing into a deep valley.
It is not that the year is bad or the people are hungry;
you direct it through commands and orders
and draw it in through the slow or rapid adjustment of prices.
Administering it thus,
it returns to us like flowing water."
Huán Gōng said:
"I wish to reduce the profits of the merchants
and increase the productivity of the farmers.
Is there a way to do this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"When grain is heavy, the myriad things are light;
when grain is light, the myriad things are heavy.
The two cannot stand in equilibrium.
Therefore, to reduce the profits of the merchants
and increase the productivity of the farmers,
I request that you raise the price of grain to three hundred per *fǔ*.
If it is like this,
the fields will be greatly opened up,
and the farmers will be encouraged in their work."
Huán Gōng said:
"Is there a way to make it heavy?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request an order for the High Officials to build granaries,
making the Ministers and Feudal Lords store one thousand *zhōng*,
ordering the High Officials to store five hundred *zhōng*,
the Ranked Officials to store one hundred *zhōng*,
and the wealthy merchants to store fifty *zhōng*.
Internally, this can serve as the state's reserve,
and externally, it can increase the productivity of the farmers."
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent."
He issued an order for the Ministers, Feudal Lords, and High Officials to build granaries.
The farmers cultivated the five grains;
the price tripled,
so the merchants lost their business,
and the farmers gained a hundredfold profit.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"Does the balance have a fixed number?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The balance has no fixed number.
Balancing means making goods sometimes high in price and sometimes low,
so they cannot remain fixed."
Huán Gōng said:
"Then the numbers of the balance cannot be regulated?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"They cannot be regulated.
If they are regulated, they become stagnant;
if they are stagnant, they become constant;
if they are constant, high and low prices do not differ;
if high and low prices do not differ,
then the myriad things cannot be obtained or put to use."
Huán Gōng said:
"Then how can one maintain the seasons?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"A year has four 'harvests,'
and the divisions have four seasons.
Thus it is said: when the farming work is about to begin,
I request that plowshares be distributed to the farmers in groups of five and ten;
this is called the harvest of spring.
When Midsummer is about to arrive,
and silk and cotton are produced;
this is called the harvest of summer.
When the Great Autumn is complete,
and the five grains are gathered;
this is called the harvest of autumn.
In Midwinter when the Yíngshì star is central,
and the women produce spinning, weaving, and sewing;
this is called the harvest of winter.
Thus a year has four harvests,
and the divisions have four seasons.
Once you have the sequence of these four,
issue commands and orders,
and the value of goods will increase tenfold or a hundredfold.
Thus goods cannot have a permanent fixity.
Therefore it is said the balance has no fixed number."
Huán Gōng said:
"Hides, trunks, sinews, horns, bamboo, arrows, feathers, hair, teeth, and leather are insufficient;
is there a way to address this?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Only the method of 'curved balancing' will suffice."
Huán Gōng said:
"How is this carried out?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request an order to establish guest houses for the merchants of the feudal lords.
Those with one chariot shall have food;
those with three chariots shall have fodder and beans;
those with five chariots shall have servants and attendants.
Then the merchants of the world will return to Qí like flowing water."
(The text is lost.)
Huán Gōng said:
"I wish to go west to pay homage to the Son of Heaven,
but the congratulatory offerings are insufficient.
Is there a method for this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request an order to fortify Yīnlǐ,
making its walls triple and its gates ninefold.
Then have the jade-workers carve stones to make *bì* disks.
Those of one foot shall be ten thousand cash;
those of eight inches shall be eight thousand;
those of seven inches shall be seven thousand;
a *guī* tablet shall be four thousand;
a *yuàn* ring shall be five hundred."
When the quantity of *bì* was prepared,
Guǎn Zǐ went west to see the Son of Heaven and said:
"The ruler of my humble state
wishes to lead the feudal lords to pay homage at the temple of the late kings
and observe the court of Zhōu.
I request an order making the feudal lords of the world
who pay homage at the temple of the late kings
and observe the court of Zhōu
use nothing but vermillion bows and stone *bì* disks.
Those who do not use vermillion bows and stone *bì* disks
shall not be allowed into the court."
The Son of Heaven permitted it, saying: "Agreed."
The command was issued to the world.
The feudal lords of the world carried gold, pearls, jade, the five grains, patterned fabrics, and currency to Qí
to obtain the stone *bì* disks.
Stone ritual discs (*shí bì*) flowed out and went to the world,
and wealth from the world flowed and went to Qí.
Thus, the state went for eight years without collecting tax registers.
This was the stratagem of Yīn Lǐ.
Above is the stratagem of the stone ritual discs.
Huán Gōng said:
"The Son of Heaven’s provisions are insufficient.
When commands and levies are issued to the world,
the feudal lords do not trust them.
Is there a way to handle this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Between the Jiāng and the Huái rivers,
there is a type of thatch with three ridges
that does not reach down to its roots.
It is named *jīng máo*.
Please have the Son of Heaven’s officials encircle, seal, and guard it.
Now, when the Son of Heaven performs the *Fēng* sacrifice at Tài Shān
and the *Shàn* sacrifice at Liáng Fù,
he should issue a command to the feudal lords of the world, saying:
'All who follow the Son of Heaven to perform the *Fēng* sacrifice at Tài Shān and the *Shàn* sacrifice at Liáng Fù
must carry a bundle of *jīng máo* to serve as a mat for the *Shàn* sacrifice.
Those who do not follow this command
shall not be permitted to participate.'"
The feudal lords of the world loaded their gold and hurried to compete for their rank.
The *jīng máo* of the Jiāng and Huái regions
naturally increased in value tenfold; its price
became a hundred pieces of gold per bundle.
Thus, within three days of the Son of Heaven taking his place,
the gold of the world flowed from all four directions and returned to Zhōu like running water.
Therefore, for seven years the Son of Heaven of Zhōu did not need to request congratulatory offerings;
this was the stratagem of the *jīng máo*.
Above is the stratagem of the *jīng máo*.
Huán Gōng said:
"I have many affairs.
I have ordered the assessment and registration of the wealthy merchants, moneylenders, and credit-granting families in my state,
to benefit my poor subjects and
farmers, so they do not lose their fundamental occupation.
Is there a way to reverse this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Only by reversing it through commands can it be done."
Huán Gōng said:
"How should it be carried out?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Please send Bīn Xūwú riding to the south,
Xí Péng riding to the north,
Níng Qī riding to the east, and
Bào Shū riding to the west.
Once the travels of these four gentlemen are set,
I, Yíwú, ask to issue a command to the four gentlemen, saying:
'You shall all, for my lord, observe the state of moneylending in the four directions,
and report to me how many thousands of households are paying interest.'"
Bào Shū rode to the west.
He returned and reported:
"The subjects of the west
border the Jì and lean against the Hé;
they are subjects of the marshes and wetlands.
They fish, hunt, and gather firewood,
steaming it to make food.
Their moneylending families,
the wealthiest have a thousand *zhōng*,
and the lesser have six or seven hundred *zhōng*.
What they lend out is one *zhōng* of interest for every *zhōng* lent.
There are over nine hundred households paying interest."
Bīn Xūwú rode to the south.
He returned and reported:
"The subjects of the south
dwell in the mountains and live in the valleys;
they are subjects who climb up and descend.
Above, they cut wood for wheel axles;
below, they gather acorns and chestnuts,
farming and hunting for food.
Their moneylending families,
the wealthiest have ten million coins,
and the lesser have six or seven million.
What they lend out is fifty percent interest.
There are over eight hundred households paying interest."
Níng Qī rode to the east.
He returned and reported:
"The subjects of the east
border the mountains and lean against the sea,
living in the valleys.
Above, they cut timber,
and they are subjects of fishing and hunting.
They process kudzu fibers for food.
Their moneylending families are the Dīng, Huì, Gāo, and Guó;
the wealthiest have five thousand *zhōng*,
and the lesser have three thousand *zhōng*.
What they lend out is five *fǔ* of interest for every *zhōng*.
There are eight or nine hundred households paying interest."
Xí Péng rode to the north.
He returned and reported:
"The subjects of the north
dwell on the plains and lean against the sea,
boiling brine to make salt;
they are subjects who build weirs across the Jì to catch fish.
They rely on gathering firewood for their food.
Their moneylending families,
the wealthiest have ten million coins,
and the lesser have six or seven million.
What they lend out
is twenty percent interest.
The subjects paying interest
number over nine hundred households."
Altogether, the moneylending families
have lent out thirty million coins,
and lent out several tens of millions of *zhōng* of grain.
The people paying interest number thirty thousand households.
The four gentlemen having finished their reports,
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"I did not expect that my lord would have subjects
where within one state there are five lords' taxations.
Under such conditions, if one wishes for the state not to be poor
and the military not to be weak,
how could that be possible?"
Huán Gōng said:
"Is there a way to handle this?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Only by reversing it through commands can it be done.
Please issue a command that all who offer congratulations must use *jù zhī lán gǔ*,
then they will naturally increase in value tenfold over their original cost.
The textiles from your Zhàn Tái
will also naturally increase in value tenfold.
Please issue a command to summon the moneylending families,
whereat your lordship shall pour wine for them,
and the Tài Zǎi shall circulate the cups.
Huán Gōng shall lift his robes and ask:
'I have many affairs
and have ordered the assessment and registration of my state.
I have heard that you lend to my poor subjects,
allowing them to fulfill the commands of their superiors.
I have *jù zhī lán gǔ*,
whose price is ten thousand coins per piece.
I wish to use these to settle the interest debts of my poor subjects,
so they have no more obligations under their contracts.'
The moneylending families all bowed their heads together and touched their foreheads to the ground, saying:
'Our lord’s concern for his subjects reaches even this far!
We request to bow twice and offer our cancellation at the hall.'
Huán Gōng shall say:
'It cannot be so.
You enable my subjects to plant their plows in the spring
and to weed their fields in the summer.
I am indebted to your virtue but have nothing to favor you with;
if I do this and you do not accept it,
I will not be at peace in my heart.'
Therefore, the moneylending families all said:
'We bow twice and accept.'
The textiles issued from Zhàn Tái
did not reach three thousand pieces,
yet they settled the interest debts of the four directions
and ensured there were no more obligations under their contracts.
When the subjects of the four directions heard of this,
fathers taught their sons
and elder brothers taught their younger brothers,
saying:
'Now, plowing the fields and clearing the grass
is the urgent matter of the superior;
can we not be diligent?
Our lord’s concern for us reaches even this far!'
This is called *fǎn zhǔn*."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"In the past, when Guǐ Dù governed a state,
he would necessarily look toward the world from all four sides.
If the world’s prices were high, he would also be high.
If the world is high while I alone am low,
one will certainly lose their state to the world."
Huán Gōng said:
"What do these words mean?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"In the past, the people of Lái were skilled at dyeing. Refined
zǐ in Lái cost only one chún zī,
and silk sashes in Lái also cost only one chún zī.
But in Zhōu, they cost ten gold pieces.
When the people of Lái learned of this,
they secretly collected and stockpiled zǐ.
Zhōu then collected horses
and appeared before the people of Lái to trade them.
Lái then established standardized prices for horses.
Thus, Lái lost its stockpiled zǐ and instead established its standard in horses.
Therefore, rely on what can be relied upon,
and take advantage of what can be taken advantage of.
This is using the world to control the world.
This is called the National Standard."
Huán Gōng said:
"In western Qí
there are floods and the people are starving,
while in eastern Qí
the harvests are abundant and grain is cheap.
I wish to use the cheap prices of the east to alleviate the high prices of the west.
Is there a way to do this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Currently, a fǔ of grain in western Qí
costs one hundred coins,
so an ōu costs twenty.
A fǔ of grain in eastern Qí
costs ten coins,
so an ōu costs two coins.
I request that an order be issued to levy thirty coins from each person,
and allow them to settle this levy with the five grains, beans, or millet.
If this is done,
then those in western Qí will output three dǒu to settle their levy,
while those in eastern Qí will output three fǔ to settle their levy.
Consequently, the grain worth ten coins per fǔ
will all fill the granaries and storehouses.
The hungry people in the west will get food,
and the cold will get clothes;
those without capital will be given old grain,
and those without seeds will be given new grain.
If this is done,
then the east and west will cover each other,
and the standards of the far and near will be leveled."
Huán Gōng said:
"I have already heard of the Methods of Balancing.
May I ask about the National Standard?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"As early spring approaches,
if the ditches and canals are obstructed and do not flow,
and the dammed waters in the valleys are not safely stored,
they will destroy houses within,
break walls,
damage fields without,
and ruin crops.
Therefore, the ruler should carefully guard the surplus goods of spring and gold,
and take action for them.
In midsummer,
when the supply of curtains, covers, clothes, and tents is insufficient,
carefully guard the surplus goods of silk and cloth,
and take action for them.
In mid-autumn,
when armor and weapons require repair
and bows and crossbows require strings,
carefully guard the surplus
goods of silk and hemp,
and take action for them.
In mid-winter,
when armor and weapons are put to use,
food provisions are insufficient,
and rewards of gold are lacking,
carefully guard the surplus
goods of the five grains and gold,
and take action for them.
Once you have guarded these surpluses,
wealthy merchants and stockpiling traders cannot act as they did before.
This is called the National Standard."
Dragons fought on the sunny side of the Mǎ Dú River
and the shady side of Niú Shān.
Guǎn Zǐ repeatedly reported to Huán Gōng, saying:
"Heaven has sent an envoy to the outskirts of your state.
Should you send your high officials in uniform, flanked by those in black robes, to meet Heaven's envoy?"
The world heard of this and said:
"How divine is Huán Gōng of Qí,
for Heaven has sent an envoy to his outskirts!"
Without waiting to raise an army, eight feudal lords came to pay court.
This is the way of taking advantage of Heaven's majesty to move the world.
Therefore, the wise command ghosts and gods,
while the foolish believe in them.
Huán Gōng ended up being seen as divine.
Guǎn Zǐ entered and reported to Huán Gōng again, saying:
"The earth shakes;
it is an omen of a plague,
and the state will have mourning.
The wind stirs;
it is an omen of a plague.
If a spear star appears in the state,
its ruler will surely be humiliated;
if a broom star appears in the state,
there will surely be bloodshed.
At the Battle of Fú Qiū,
where the broom star appeared,
the enemies of the world were surely subdued.
Now a broom star has appeared in the celestial division of Qí.
I request that an order be issued for the meritorious officials and noble families to attend court,
and a command be issued throughout the state saying:
'A broom star has appeared.
I fear subduing the world's enemies.
Those who have the five grains, beans, millet, cloth, silk, or fine fabrics
should not dare to keep them for themselves.
The state is about to have a major event;
I request to take them at a fair price.' The families of meritorious officials,
and the common people all presented their grains, beans, millet, and coins,
and surrendered their wealth and goods
to assist the ruler's major event.
This is called the way of taking advantage of Heaven's disasters to seek the people's wealth.
Huán Gōng said:
"The high officials are hoarding their wealth and not releasing it,
letting the five grains rot without distributing them."
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request an order to summon the Grand Officer of Chéng Yáng and reprimand him."
Huán Gōng said:
"Why?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"(Say to him:) 'Grand Officer of Chéng Yáng,
your favorites are dressed in fine hemp and silk,
your geese and ducks eat leftover grain,
you have the music of Qí bells and drums,
and play flutes and pipes.
Yet those of the same surname are not allowed in,
and your uncles, aunts,
and near and distant brothers
are all cold and cannot get clothes,
or hungry and cannot get food.
You wish to be completely loyal to me—is that possible?
Therefore, do not see me again.'
Strip him of his position,
and shut his gates so he cannot come out."
The families of meritorious officials
then all vied to open their stockpiles,
put out their wealth and goods,
and give them to their near and distant brothers.
Thinking it was not enough,
they also gathered the poor, sick, orphaned, widowed, and elderly in the state who could not feed themselves, and all were provided for.
Thus, Huán Gōng promoted benevolence and established righteousness;
the families of meritorious officials
cared for their brothers
and were close to their kin,
and the state had no starving people.
This is called the Tactics of Mutual Connection.
Huán Gōng said:
"In the Battle of Zhēng Qiū,
many people borrowed money
and incurred debt with interest
to provide for the urgent needs of the superior
and to meet the ruler's demands.
I wish to restore their livelihoods and properties.
How can this be harmonized?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Only the Tactics of Mutual Connection will do."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
He ordered the surrounding zhōu districts saying:
"Mark the homes of those who lent money;
whitewash their gates
and heighten their lǘ neighborhood gates."
The masters of the zhōu districts, holding tally-strips, said:
"The ruler will soon send envoys."
Huán Gōng sent eight envoys, holding ritual jade disks, to visit and pay respects to them,
providing for their needs of salt and vegetables.
The families who had lent money all touched their heads to the ground in greeting and asked:
"Why have we received this?"
The messenger said:
"The ruler’s command says:
'I have heard that the *Shī* says:
"The joyful and easygoing gentleman
is the parent of the people."
I have faced the Battle of Zhēngqiū.
I heard that you lent to my poor subjects,
enabling them to meet my urgent needs
and satisfying my requirements.
You enabled my subjects to have tools for planting in spring
and tools for weeding in summer, while also fulfilling their duties to the state;
this was your effort.
Therefore, I present a ritual jade disk to offer you an appointment,
to provide for your daily needs.
Thus, you are truly a parent to the people.'"
The families that had lent money all tore up their vouchers and scraped clean their records,
opened their storehouses,
brought out their wealth and goods,
and used them to relieve the poor and sick.
Because they distributed their former wealth,
the capital was greatly provided for;
this was the strategy of Zhēngqiū.
This is called "Harmonious Calculations."
Huán Gōng said:
"The people of the four suburbs are poor,
while the merchants are wealthy.
I wish to reduce the wealth of the merchants to benefit the people of the four suburbs.
How should this be done?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"I request that you issue an order to divert the waters of the Wòluò River
and channel them through the area of Kàngzhuāng."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
Before the order had been in effect for a year,
the people of the suburbs became abundantly wealthy,
while the merchants became visibly poorer.
Huán Gōng summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"When the Wòluò River was diverted
and channeled through Kàngzhuāng,
the refuse and waste from the butchers and brewers made the flowing water rich.
Then the gadflies, giant dragonflies, and small birds like kingfishers and swallows
all gathered there.
It became suitable for drinking at dusk;
this is a pleasure of being on the water.
When merchants store goods, they sell to find buyers
and buy to obtain stock.
But before the market was finished, they would abandon their stalls
to go after the gadflies and giant dragonflies.
Young men with new five-foot-high caps
requested to carry slings and hold stones to go to the water,
shooting the kingfishers and swallows
until sunset.
Thus, they sold cheaply and bought at high prices.
Since the people of the four suburbs bought cheaply,
why would they not be wealthy?
And why would the merchants not be poor?"
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng said:
"The people of the five thoroughfares
are in decline, mostly wearing tattered clothes and worn-out shoes.
I wish to make the prices of silk,
cloth, raw silk, and floss cheap.
Is there a way to do this?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"I request that you issue an order to prune the tree branches along the roads
so that there is not an inch of shade."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
Before the order had been in effect for a year,
the people of the five thoroughfares mostly wore silk and intact shoes.
Huán Gōng summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"When the trees along the roads
had not yet been pruned,
the people of the five thoroughfares,
men and women who were fond of each other,
when they went to the market,
would finish their business
and meet under the trees,
talking all day without returning home.
When the men and women were in their prime,
pushing and pulling carts,
they would meet under the trees,
laughing, playing, and jumping,
staying all day without returning home.
Fathers and elder brothers would meet under the trees
to engage in profound discussions,
staying all day without returning home.
Thus, the fields were not plowed,
the five grains were not sown,
hemp and mulberry were not planted,
and cocoons and threads were not processed.
When three members of a single household did not return home,
how could the prices of silk, cloth, raw silk, and floss not be high?"
Huán Gōng said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng said:
"Grain is cheap,
and I fear that the five grains will go to the other lords.
I wish to store them for the common people.
Is there a way to do this?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Today, I, Yíwú, passed through the market
and saw two families that had newly built granaries.
My lord, please present ritual jade disks and offer them appointments."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
After the order had been in effect for half a year,
the common people heard of it,
and they abandoned their other tasks
to build granaries for storing beans, millet, and the five grains; more than half did so.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"What is the reason for this?"
Guǎn Zǐ said: "Regarding the two families that built granaries,
you presented ritual jade disks and offered them appointments.
Their fame was made manifest throughout the capital,
and no one in the capital failed to hear of it.
Thus, in their relationship with their superiors, the people find that they can achieve fame among the commoners without official merit;
their merit is established and their fame is achieved.
Below, they fill their granaries,
and above, they provide for you as the ruler.
With one action, both fame and reality are attained.
Why would the people not do it?"
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"May I ask about the management of the 'King's Calculations' from beginning to end?
May I hear it?"
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"The morning of the first month
is the beginning of grain.
One hundred days from the solstice
is the beginning of glutinous and non-glutinous millet.
The ninth month is when the harvest is gathered,
which is the beginning of barley and wheat."
Guǎn Zǐ asked Huán Gōng:
"I venture to ask, how many li is the square of Qí?"
Huán Gōng said:
"It is five hundred li square."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"The land of the Yīnyōng Great Wall
accounts for one-third of the state of Qí;
it is not land where grain grows.
Huìhǎi, Zhuāng, and Lóngxià
account for one-fourth of Qí.
They are remote from morning to evening,
and the unusable parts of Qí's territory account for one-fifth;
these are not land where grain grows.
If so, then am I not a ruler who relies on others for food?"
Huán Gōng stood up abruptly and said:
"If so, what should be done about it?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Move them with words;
influence them with rhetoric;
this can be the foundation of the state.
Furthermore, if you focus on the management of currency,
then the merchants alone will control the state's profit;
if you focus on the management of grain,
then the farmers alone will control the state's stability.
If you initiate words and control rhetoric,
then regarding the flow around you,
you alone will follow..."
As for the beginning of things,
I have already seen it;
as for the end of things,
I have already seen it;
as for the price of things,
I have already seen it.
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"The sunny side of the Chángchéng is
Lǔ.
The shady side of the Chángchéng is
Qí.
Having suffered three defeats,
killed two high ministers of the ruler,
and yet stabilized the Altars of Soil and Grain, I
see that these were all cases of being enfeoffed with the land of Hútù.
Thus, mountain land is the mountain;
water land is the marsh;
and the place where fuel and fodder grow is the alkaline wasteland."
The Duke said:
"For a ruler who relies on food
and my land,
is there also a Way?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Guard its Three Origins."
The Duke asked:
"What are the Three Origins?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"If the ruler guards cloth,
then levy a tax on hemp;
its price will increase tenfold,
and cloth will increase its price fiftyfold.
This is the calculation.
If the ruler uses weaving to levy a tax, levy it on silk thread.
Before levying on silk thread,
manage the silk and the weaving; its price will again increase tenfold.
In this manner, it is called the levy on the five grains.
Therefore, when levying on cloth, manage the thread;
when levying on grain, manage the mountains;
when levying on the six domestic animals, manage the techniques.
Levy on the end and the beginning of things and be skilled at controlling them through words."
The Duke said:
"Excellent."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Use the state as one to levy on the ministers;
on the right, guard ten thousand taels of cloth,
and on the right, the levy on hemp will increase its price fortyfold.
Cloth will increase its price fiftyfold.
Your Grace can use the heavy cloth to determine the prices of the feudal lords.
In this way, you will have twenty times the wealth of Qí.
Therefore, for those who nimbly surpass others in price, grain, and livestock management,
then things will surpass the assistance of the four seasons.
One who is good at governing a state
guards the wealth of his state,
stirs it with highs and lows,
and pours it with slowness and speed,
so that one can be made into a hundred.
Without ever seeking levies from the people,
and using resources as if they were rivers or seas,
when it ends, there is a beginning again.
This is called guarding things and controlling all under Heaven."
The Duke asked:
"In that case, can nothingness be made into existence?
Can poverty be made into wealth?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"When things are born, they do not yet have form,
yet Kings and Hegemons establish their achievements there.
Therefore, if you seek people through people,
then people become heavy.
If you seek things through calculations,
then things become heavy."
The Duke asked:
"What do these words mean?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"If you take the whole state as one,
then there is no wealth;
if you take the whole state as ten,
then there are a hundred.
Thus I will control them with slowness and speed,
as if the left hand were giving to the right
or the right hand were giving to the left.
In this way, the internal and external are not cramped,
and throughout one's life there is no blame.
Kings and Hegemons do not seek from people
but seek from the end and beginning,
the high and low of the four seasons,
and the slowness and speed of orders—that is all.
A spring may be exhausted;
ghosts and spirits may have a rest.
But guarding the end and beginning of things
is inexhaustible throughout one's life.
This is called the 'investigation of the source.'"
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"How should the 'light and heavy' be applied?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Since the time of Fú Xī managing the state,
there has never been one who could achieve kingship without using the 'light and heavy.'"
The Duke asked:
"What do you mean?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"When Fú Xī arose, he created the Six Laws
to welcome the Yīn and Yáng;
he created the calculations of nine-times-nine
to harmonize with the Way of Heaven,
and all under Heaven was transformed by it.
When Shén Nóng arose, he planted the five grains on the sunny side of Qí Shān.
The people of the Jiǔ Zhōu
then knew of grain for food,
and all under Heaven was transformed by it.
When Suì Rén arose, he drilled wood to produce fire
to cook meat and fish,
so that when the people ate them, they had no stomach ailments,
and all under Heaven was transformed by it.
During the kingship of Huáng Dì,
he cleared the mountains and exhausted the marshes.
During the kingship of Yǒu Yú,
he burned the overgrown thickets
and cut down the various pests
to create benefits for the people;
he mounded the earth to make the Altars of Soil,
and placed wood to mark the village gates,
so the people began to know ritual.
At that time,
the people had no resentment or disobedience,
and all under Heaven was transformed by it.
During the kingship of the Xià people,
they dug twenty canals externally and seventeen reservoirs,
dredged the Sān Jiāng,
excavated the Wǔ Hú,
and channeled the waters of the four rivers
to evaluate the heights of the Jiǔ Zhōu
and manage the nine marshes.
The people then knew how to build city walls, gates, and houses,
and all under Heaven was transformed by it.
During the kingship of the Yīn people,
they established stables and pens,
and broke in oxen and horses
to create benefits for the people,
and all under Heaven was transformed by it.
During the kingship of the Zhōu people,
they followed the Six Laws
and harmonized Yīn and Yáng,
and all under Heaven was transformed by it."
The Duke asked:
"In that case, what should the king of the current age do?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Use them together, but do not exhaust them all."
The Duke asked:
"What do you mean?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The Way of Emperors and Kings is complete;
it cannot be added to.
Your Grace should simply practice righteousness."
The Duke asked:
"How does one practice righteousness?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"The Son of Heaven is young and weak,
while the feudal lords are overbearing and strong,
and the missions and offerings are not being sent up.
Your Grace should support the weak, strengthen the broken lines of succession,
and lead the feudal lords to restore the sacrifices of the Zhōu house."
The Duke said:
"Excellent."
Huán Gōng said:
"The relationship of Lǔ and Liáng to Qí
is like a thousand valleys,
like a bee's sting,
or like the lips to the teeth.
Now I wish to subdue Lǔ and Liáng;
how should I proceed?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“The custom of the people of Lǔ and Liáng is to wear tí.
If Your Lordship wears tí,
and orders your attendants to wear it,
the people will follow and wear it.
You should then order that Qí shall not produce it,
so it must be sought from Lǔ and Liáng.
In this way, Lǔ and Liáng will abandon their farming and produce tí.”
Huán Gōng said: “Agreed.”
He then had robes made south of Tàishān,
and wore them ten days later.
Guǎn Zǐ told the merchants of Lǔ and Liáng:
“If you bring me one thousand bolts of tí,
I will reward you with three hundred jīn of gold.
For every hundred bolts brought, you will get thirty jīn of gold.”
Thus, Lǔ and Liáng did not tax their people, and their financial resources were sufficient.
When the rulers of Lǔ and Liáng heard of this,
they taught their people to produce tí.
After thirteen months, Guǎn Zǐ sent people to Lǔ and Liáng.
Among the people within the city walls of Lǔ and Liáng,
the roads were thick with dust,
so that one could not see another at ten paces.
Wearing straw sandals, they followed closely behind one another;
the hubs of their carriages rubbed together, and the cavalry
moved in continuous files.
Guǎn Zǐ said:
“Lǔ and Liáng can now be brought down.”
The Duke asked:
“How?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Your Lordship should wear silk,
and lead the people to abandon tí. Close the passes,
and do not allow diplomatic communication with Lǔ and Liáng.”
The Duke said:
“Agreed.”
Ten months later,
Guǎn Zǐ sent people to Lǔ and Liáng.
The people of Yú Liáng
were starving and following one another in hunger;
the official levies
could not be provided to the superiors.
The rulers of Lǔ and Liáng
immediately ordered their people to abandon tí and return to farming. However, grain
cannot be harvested in only three months.
The people of Lǔ and Liáng
bought grain for a thousand coins,
while Qí sold it for ten coins.
After twenty-four months,
six-tenths of the people of Lǔ and Liáng had defected to Qí.
After three years,
the rulers of Lǔ and Liáng requested to submit.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“The people are hungry and have no food,
cold and have no clothes;
the official levies
cannot be provided to the superiors;
the houses leak and are not repaired,
and the walls are ruined and not rebuilt.
What should be done?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Prune the branches of the roadside trees.”
Huán Gōng said:
“Agreed.”
He ordered the Zuǒ Yòu Bó to prune the branches of the roadside trees.
The Zuǒ Yòu Bó received the order, and the branches of the roadside trees were cleared.
In that year,
the people wore plain cloth;
they were pure within and substantial without; the official
levies
could be provided to the superiors;
those whose houses leaked were able to repair them,
and those whose walls were ruined were able to rebuild them.
The Duke summoned Guǎn Zǐ and asked:
“What is the reason for this?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Qí
is a land of the Yí and Lái tribes.
If one tree allows a hundred chariots to rest beneath it,
it is because it was not pruned.
Numerous birds would dwell upon it;
able-bodied young men with slings and pellets would stay beneath it,
not returning all day long.
The elders would lean against the branches and converse,
not returning all day long.
Those returning from the market would also loiter and gaze,
not returning all day long.
Now that we have pruned the branches of the roadside trees,
at midday there is not an inch of shade.
Those coming and going stay only a short time;
travelers walk briskly;
the elders return and manage their livelihoods,
and the able-bodied return and work on their professions.
Since those subjects have returned from their ‘three non-returns,’
this is why the villages do not lack resources.”
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“Lái and Jǔ are bordering our scrubland;
what should be done about them?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“The mountains of Lái and Jǔ produce firewood.
My Lord, you should lead the commoner soldiers
to cast gold from Zhuāngshān to make currency,
and pay a high price for the firewood of Lái.”
When the ruler of Lái heard of this,
he told his attendants:
“Gold currency
is what people value.
Firewood
is a unique product of our state.
By using the unique product of our state
to exhaust the heavy treasures of Qí,
then Qí can be annexed.”
Lái then abandoned its farming and produced firewood.
Guǎn Zǐ then ordered Xí Péng to have the people return to farming.
Two years later,
Huán Gōng stopped buying firewood.
The price of grain in Lái and Jǔ reached three hundred and seventy,
while Qí sold it for ten coins.
Seven-tenths of the people of Lái and Jǔ surrendered to Qí.
After twenty-eight months,
the rulers of Lái and Jǔ requested to submit.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
“Chǔ
is a powerful state east of the mountains,
and its people are skilled in the ways of combat.
If I raise an army to attack it,
I fear our strength may not prevail.
If our troops are exhausted by Chǔ
and our achievements are not completed for Zhōu,
what should be done?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“Then deal with them using the ways of combat.”
The Duke said:
“What do you mean?”
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
“My Lord should buy their deer at high prices.”
Huán Gōng then built a walled city of a hundred lǐ
and sent people to Chǔ to buy live deer.
A live deer from Chǔ cost eighty thousand coins each.
Guǎn Zǐ then ordered Huán Gōng to manage the economic balance with the people,
and stored away six-tenths of the grain.
He ordered the Marshal of the Left Bó Gōng to lead commoner laborers to cast coins at Zhuāngshān.
He ordered the Grand Official Wáng Yì to carry twenty million coins to seek live deer in Chǔ.
When the King of Chǔ heard this,
he told his Chancellor:
“Gold and coins
are what people value,
what a state relies on to survive,
and what an enlightened ruler uses to reward those with merit.
Birds and beasts
are pests to the masses
and what an enlightened king casts out and chases away.
Now Qí uses its heavy treasures to buy our pests at high prices;
this is surely a blessing for Chǔ!
Heaven is using Qí to favor Chǔ.
Tell my people
to seek live deer urgently
to exhaust the treasures of Qí.”
The people of Chǔ then abandoned their farming and hunted deer.
Guǎn Zǐ told the merchants of Chǔ:
“If you bring me twenty live deer,
I will reward you with one hundred jīn of gold.
For ten times that amount arriving, you will get one thousand jīn of gold.”
Consequently, Chǔ did not tax its people and had sufficient financial resources.
The men of Chǔ stayed out in the fields,
and the women stayed on the roads.
Xí Péng instructed the people to store grain at five times the price;
Chǔ used live deer to store money at five times the value.
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"Chǔ can now be brought down."
The Duke said:
"How?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Chǔ’s money is valued fivefold.
Their ruler will become self-satisfied
and neglect agriculture.
Because money is worth five times as much,
this makes Chǔ appear strong."
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
He then ordered the closure of the passes and ceased the exchange of envoys with Chǔ.
The King of Chǔ indeed became self-satisfied and neglected agriculture.
Grain cannot be obtained in just three months;
the price of grain in Chǔ reached four hundred.
Qí then ordered people to carry grain and stay to the south of Qiān;
four-tenths of the Chǔ people surrendered to Qí.
In three years, Chǔ submitted.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"What does the state of Dài produce?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"Dài produces
white fox furs.
You, Duke, should buy them at a high price."
Guǎn Zǐ said:
"The white fox responds to the changes of Yīn and Yáng,
appearing only once every six months.
If you buy them at a high price,
the people of Dài will forget how difficult they are to obtain;
delighted by your high-priced purchases,
they will surely lead one another to seek them.
Thus, Qí's gold and money need not be exhausted,
but the people of Dài will surely abandon their basic occupation and dwell within the mountains and forests.
When Lí Zhī hears of this,
they will surely invade their north.
If Lí Zhī invades their north,
Dài will surely return to Qí.
The Duke said: 'Now let us order Qí to carry gold and money and go there.'"
Huán Gōng said:
"Agreed."
He immediately ordered the Grand Official Wáng Shī to lead men and followers north,
carrying gold and money
to the valleys of Dài,
to seek white fox furs.
The King of Dài heard of this
and immediately told his minister:
"The reason Dài is weaker than Lí Zhī
is that we have no gold or money.
Now Qí is using gold and money to seek white fox furs;
this is Dài's good fortune.
Quickly order the people to seek white fox furs
to obtain Qí's currency;
I will then use it to attract the people of Lí Zhī."
The people of Dài indeed abandoned their basic occupation
and dwelt within the mountains and forests
to seek white fox furs.
For twenty-four months, they did not obtain a single one.
Lí Zhī heard of this
and invaded their north.
The King of Dài heard of this and was greatly afraid.
He then led his soldiers to defend the valleys of Dài.
Lí Zhī then invaded their north;
the King then led his soldiers and wished to submit to Qí.
Qí did not lose a single coin;
diplomatic relations were maintained for three years and Dài submitted.
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zǐ:
"As for the technique of using grain to control Héng Shān,
how is it done?"
Guǎn Zǐ replied:
"You, Duke, should have people buy the mechanical tools of Héng Shān at a high price and then sell them.
Yān and Dài will surely follow you and buy them.
When Qín and Zhào hear of this,
they will surely compete with you for them.
The mechanical tools of Héng Shān
will surely double in price.
When the whole world competes for them,
the price of Héng Shān’s tools
will surely increase tenfold or more."
The Duke said:
"Agreed."
He then sent people to Héng Shān to seek and buy mechanical tools,
not daring to dispute their high price.
Qí purchased mechanical tools in Héng Shān for ten months.
When Yān and Dài heard of this,
they indeed sent people to Héng Shān to seek and buy mechanical tools.
Yān and Dài purchased for three months.
When the state of Qín heard of this,
it indeed sent people to Héng Shān to seek and buy mechanical tools.
The Lord of Héng Shān told his minister:
"The whole world is competing for my mechanical tools;
let their price be raised twenty times or more."
The people of Héng Shān
abandoned their basic occupation and refined the skill of making mechanical tools.
Qí then ordered Xí Péng to transport grain from Zhào.
In Zhào, grain was sold for fifteen;
Xí Péng bought it at fifty per dàn.
When the world heard of this,
they carried grain and went to Qí.
Qí purchased mechanical tools for seventeen months
and purchased grain for five months;
then it closed its passes and ceased the exchange of envoys with Héng Shān.
Yān, Dài, Qín, and Zhào then withdrew their envoys and returned.
The mechanical tools of Héng Shān were exhausted.
Lǔ annexed the south of Héng Shān,
and Qí annexed the north of Héng Shān.
Internally realizing they had no mechanical tools to face the two enemies,
they surrendered the state and submitted to Qí.
Pure spirit gives birth to the heart,
the heart gives birth to the compass,
the compass gives birth to the square,
the square gives birth to the quadrilateral,
the quadrilateral gives birth to the upright,
the upright gives birth to the calendar,
the calendar gives birth to the four seasons,
and the four seasons give birth to all things.
The Sage follows this and regulates it;
the Way is then all-encompassing.
Starting from the winter solstice,
count forty-six days;
winter ends and spring begins.
The Son of Heaven goes out forty-six lǐ to the east of his capital and builds an altar;
he wears green robes and a green crown,
inserts the royal jade tablet,
and wears the royal mirror belt.
He holds court with the feudal lords, ministers, grand officials, and scholars,
and inspects the common people.
This is called "Sacrificing to the Day,"
and the sacrifice is performed with fish.
He issues an order saying:
"Give life and do not kill;
reward and do not punish;
do not decide criminal cases,
until the year is out."
He teaches the people to gather firewood and drill for fire,
to plaster the stoves and clear the wells;
these are the means to ensure the longevity of the people.
Plowshares, hand-plows, weeders, hoes,
sickles, spades, scythes, forks,
irrigation tools, and tool-bindings—these are the means to manage the affairs of spring and summer,
and they must be prepared. He teaches the people to prepare wine and food,
which are for the purpose of filial piety and respect.
A person born without father or mother
is called an orphan;
one without wife or children
is called an old widower;
one without husband or children
is called an old widow.
These three types of people
gather at the government offices and are numerous.
Whether they are able to work
or unable to work,
they are fed as specified without being neglected.
Providing for many is a merit;
providing for few is a crime.
Thus, there are no beggars on the roads.
If there are beggars on the roads,
it is the crime of the Prime Minister.
This is the spring order of the Son of Heaven.
Starting from the winter solstice,
count ninety-two days;
this is called the arrival of spring.
The Son of Heaven goes out ninety-two lǐ to the east of his capital
and builds an altar,
holding court with the feudal lords, ministers, grand officials, and scholars.
Inspect the common people,
calling it the Sacrifice to the Stars (Jì Xīng).
Within ten days,
no maiden remains indoors,
and no traveler is on the road.
If there are those who do not plant or cultivate,
they are called harmful people;
they violate the Earth below,
and they violate the Heavens above,
being called disobedient people;
in the village they are of the lowest rank,
and in the army they are of the lowest order,
being called laborers.
If for three years they do not plant, the ruler shall command them.
This is the Spring Ordinance of the Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ).
Starting from the Spring Equinox (Chūn Rì Zhì),
count forty-six days,
and spring ends while summer begins.
The Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) wears yellow and stays in quietude,
granting audience to the feudal lords (Zhū Hóu), ministers (Qīng), grand masters (Dà Fū), and the ranks of scholars (Liè Shì),
inspecting the common people,
and issuing proclamations and orders, saying:
"Do not gather large crowds,
do not use large fires,
do not cut down large trees
(nor execute great ministers),
do not clear large mountains,
and do not destroy large marshes.
To destroy these three greats brings harm to the state."
This is the Summer Prohibition of the Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ).
Starting from the Spring Equinox (Chūn Rì Zhì),
count ninety-two days,
which is called the Summer Solstice (Xià Zhì),
and the wheat ripens.
The Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) sacrifices at the Great Ancestral Shrine (Tài Zōng),
and the ritual offering consists of wheat.
Wheat
is the first of the grains;
the Great Ancestral Shrine
is the origin of the clan.
Those of the same clan enter,
while those of different clans stay outside.
All must fast and purify. Large timbers
are brought out to sacrifice to the Royal Mother (Wáng Mǔ).
This is how the Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) presides over beginnings and observes taboos.
Starting from the Summer Solstice (Xià Zhì),
count forty-six days,
and summer ends while autumn begins,
and the broomcorn millet ripens.
The Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) sacrifices at the Grand Ancestor (Tài Zǔ) shrine,
and the ritual offering consists of broomcorn millet.
Broomcorn millet
is the finest of grains.
The Grand Ancestor
is the weightiest matter of the state.
Those with great merit belong to the Grand Ancestor (Tài Zǔ),
those with small merit belong to the Lesser Ancestor (Xiǎo Zǔ),
and those without merit have no ancestor.
Those with merit all take their positions according to their rank and perform the libations,
while those without merit observe from the outside.
The Ancestral Sacrifice
is a sacrifice for merit,
not a sacrifice for kinship.
This is how the Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) distinguishes the noble from the base and rewards those with merit.
Starting from the Summer Solstice (Xià Zhì),
count ninety-two days, which is called the Autumn Equinox (Qiū Zhì).
At the Autumn Equinox, the grain ripens.
The Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) sacrifices at Tài Ruǐ;
he travels west from his capital
one hundred and thirty-eight lǐ to an altar,
wearing white robes and a white cap,
inserting a jade tablet into his sash,
wearing a tin mirror at his belt,
playing the melodies of the xūn and chí flutes,
and striking the sounds of metal and stone instruments.
He grants audience to the feudal lords (Zhū Hóu), ministers (Qīng), grand masters (Dà Fū), and the ranks of scholars (Liè Shì),
inspects the common people,
and calls it the Sacrifice to the Moon (Jì Yuè),
with a pig as the sacrificial victim.
He issues proclamations and orders:
Punish and do not reward,
take away and do not give,
and in criminal cases, execute and do not spare;
for the crimes of the whole year,
there shall be no pardons.
One who calculates the actual cattle and horses in the fields is a king.
This is the Autumn Accounting of the Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ).
Starting from the Autumn Equinox (Qiū Rì Zhì),
count forty-six days,
and autumn ends while winter begins.
The Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) wears black robes and a black cap and stays in quietude,
granting audience to the feudal lords (Zhū Hóu), ministers (Qīng), grand masters (Dà Fū), and the ranks of scholars (Liè Shì),
inspecting the common people,
and issuing proclamations and orders, saying:
"Do not use large fires,
do not clear large mountains,
do not dam large waters,
and do not offend the majesty of Heaven."
This is the Winter Prohibition of the Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ).
Starting from the Autumn Equinox (Qiū Rì Zhì),
count ninety-two days.
The Son of Heaven (Tiān Zǐ) travels north ninety-two lǐ to an altar,
wearing black robes and a black cap,
grants audience to the feudal lords (Zhū Hóu), ministers (Qīng), grand masters (Dà Fū), and the ranks of scholars (Liè Shì),
and calls it the Distribution of Labor (Fā Yáo).
Urge the mountain-dwellers to cut and fell timber
and prepare tools and equipment;
urge the marsh-dwellers to gather firewood and reeds
to ensure sufficient stores.
After three months,
all shall exchange what they have for what they lack.
This is called the Great Circulation
of the three months' stores.
Whenever it is time to urge plowing but one does not plow,
the people will become lawless;
such is the harm of not plowing.
When it is proper to weed but one does not weed,
all kinds of grasses will remain,
and the people will barely survive;
such is the harm of not weeding.
When it is proper to harvest but one does not harvest,
wind and rain will arise,
the five grains (Wǔ Gǔ) will be depleted,
and the scholars and people will be scattered and lost;
such is the harm of not harvesting.
When it is proper to store but one does not store,
the mists will be sweltering,
things that should die will live,
and things that should hibernate will cry out;
such is the harm of not storing.
Setting the plowshare is equivalent to drawing a crossbow,
using the weeding hoe is equivalent to using swords and halberds,
the water-scoop is equivalent to side armor,
and the straw cape and hat are equivalent to shields and ramparts.
Therefore, when the tools for plowing are ready, the equipment for war is prepared.
The chapter is lost.
